# Tiwas Adventure Readiness Audit — Beyond the Vale of Madness (GURPS) as Benchmark

## 1. Executive Summary

This audit inventories all mechanical demands actually exercised or assumed by Beyond the Vale of Madness — GURPS (a solo “choose-your-path” dungeon crawl with 2 featured combats), then evaluates whether the current Tiwas baseline (Canonical Core + Ruled non-canonical subsystems in the supplied corpus) can support those demands without inventing new Tiwas mechanics.

Bottom line A partial Tiwas playtest is possible now, but a full-fidelity playtest of the adventure’s mechanical intent is blocked primarily by missing Tiwas content-authoring layers (S-12 creatureNPC stats, equipment tagsitems, and especially magic) and by incomplete S-3 gated-tier effect enumeration (needed for fearterror, darkness penalties, grapples, corrosive ongoing damage, etc., unless treated as pure narrative).

### Key blockers (highest impact)
 Blocker  Type  Why it blocks 
---------
 S-12 creatureNPC stat blocks not table-ready  Missing subsystemcontent (per corpus Part C.1)  Adventure requires at least two hostile monsters with tactical behavior Ice Troll and Blood Man (and implied wolvesghouls). Without S-12 content, Tiwas cannot run the fights mechanically. 
 Magic  spells (pyromancer pregens reference GURPS Magic)  Missing subsystem  The adventure explicitly offers a spellcasting pregen and refers to GURPS Magic effects; Tiwas baseline has no magic implementation. 
 S-3 gated-tier effect contents not enumerated  Design-stage dependency  Many adventure outcomes imply conditions (fear), positioning, grapplehold, ongoing corrosive damage, darkness combat penalties, etc. Tiwas has the menu skeleton (DEC-023+) but not the concrete effect list for these. 
 Equipmentencumbrancewealth economy  Missing subsystem (mostly)  Adventure uses ST requirements, weapon damage profiles, weights, loot value, and carrying limits for tapestries. Tiwas has no canonical equipment economyencumbrance rules in provided baseline. 

### What is playtestable now (useful benchmark)
- Core Test Transaction (DEC-006) for climbing, search, willpower, perception-like checks, tracking, forced entry, etc.
- Difficulty grades as additive effective-skill modifiers (DEC-063–066).
- Opposed contests (S-1, DEC-013), applicable to stealth vs perception in principle (but requires statted opponents).
- HPMPPhysical Energy cost + Overflow (DEC-007 + DEC-007.A) as a harsh risk model for repeated tests and “exhaustion”.

---

## 2. Audit Objective and Method

### Objective
Use the adventure as an external benchmark to determine whether Tiwas currently provides the mechanics needed to run the adventure’s full mechanical surface area, and to identify which Tiwas subsystems are blocking that.

### Method (systems-engineering style)
1. Extract mechanical requirements from the adventure text (paragraph triggers, roll calls, combat procedures, item mechanics, environmental hazards, and any implied mechanics such as darkness penalties and fear).
2. Normalize resolution treat every GURPS skillattribute roll as requiring a standard Tiwas Core Test (DEC-006), not a GURPS-like engine.
3. For each requirement, assess
   - Tiwas capability (Canonical  Ruled  Open)
   - Readiness category (per prompt)
   - Blocking significance
   - Remaining work (without inventing mechanics; only identify missing decisionscontent)

Authoritative sources used
- Adventure parsed PDF text provided (19 pages of content; includes pregens and treasure table).
- Tiwas baseline `Tiwas-Alpha-Playtest-Corpus-2026-09-01.md` (Core Locked + Ruled DEC material; explicit “not table-ready” list).

---

## 8. Tiwas Readiness Assessment (Against This Benchmark)

### 8.1 What Tiwas can already benchmark well here
- High-frequency risky testing the adventure’s many small checks are a good stress test of Cost=Roll and Overflow immutability, and will rapidly surface whether players “spam tests” or become resource-starved.
- Difficulty handling many “-3-5untrained” style calls are a good benchmark for S-8’s effective-skill modifiers.

### 8.2 What this benchmark shows Tiwas is not ready to validate
- Creature combat loop without S-12 and an equipmentattack model, the adventure cannot validate Tiwas combat as a product experience.
- Conditions as gameplay feardarknessgrapplingongoing damage are central to the Blood Man scene; Tiwas cannot currently express these as settled mechanics.

---

## 9. Development Priorities Exposed by the Adventure

Ranked by “unblocks full playtest of this specific module”

1. S-12 tabletop creature stat-block method + author the two monsters
   - Minimum deliverable simple GM-run stat blocks with Tiwas Skill values needed for contests and effects.
2. Equipment + attack payload model (even a minimal alpha layer)
   - Must support melee weapon attack, ranged crossbow (single bolt), basic armor notion (even if tag-only), shield handling if relevant.
3. S-3 gated-tier effect content enumeration (at least for)
   - Fearterror condition
   - Darknessvisibility condition
   - GrappleBreak Hold
   - Ongoing damage (corrosive “per time-step”) or a Tiwas-native equivalent
4. Defense mitigation semantics (S-6 concretization)
   - Define what outcomes a successful defense produces for Injury and Conditions.
5. Environmental hazard procedure (coldexhaustion)
   - Could be expressed as a hazard repeatedly forcing Body-domain tests, with Overflow doing the “damage” work; but needs a settled cadencetrigger policy.

Magic is also major, but optional if you agree the benchmark run will use a non-magical Tiwas character rather than the provided Enfys pregen.

---

## 10. Conclusions

- Playtestable Now (partial) exploration checks, navigation, climbing, search, locked doors, and resource attrition using the Core Test and S-8 difficulty.
- Not fully playtestable the adventure’s defining scenes (Ice Troll and Blood Man) cannot be run mechanically in Tiwas without S-12 content, an equipmentcombat payload layer, and conditiongrappledarknessfear effect definitions.
- The module is therefore a strong benchmark for prioritizing S-12 creature authoring + minimal combatequipment + concrete condition effects.

## 12. Explicit Assumptions  Unresolved Questions

1. Difficulty tier numeric values are not shown in the provided excerpt; this audit assumes they exist but requires a mapping policy from adventure modifiers (-3, -5, etc.) to Tiwas named grades.
2. Combat time model (roundsseconds) is not defined in Tiwas baseline; therefore “per second” ongoing damage (Blood Seep) cannot be represented without new mechanics.
3. The audit treats GURPS “damage dice” outputs as requiring an adaptation decision (how to express hazardattack magnitude in Tiwas) because Tiwas baseline does not define a dice-based damage model.
4. Skill cataloging Tiwas allows creating skills via the cap formula mechanism, but no canonical skill list exists; mapping “ClimbingLockpickingetc.” to Tiwas skills is treated as adaptation content work, not a missing Tiwas rule.
5. Using pregenerated characters the provided pregens are GURPS-specific; Tiwas would require Tiwas-native character builds. This audit treats that as adaptation content, except for the spellcaster whose functionality depends on missing magic rules.

If you provide (a) the S-8 difficulty tier numeric modifier table, and (b) any existing draft for a minimal Tiwas combat payload model (even if non-canonical), I can re-run the assessment to separate “missing subsystem” from “mapping required” more sharply for combat, hazards, and equipment.

## btvmadness-adapt-report-chatgpt-5-5-high-1.md

```markdown
# Tiwas Adventure Readiness Audit  
## *Beyond the Vale of Madness — GURPS* as a Tiwas Benchmark

**Audit role:** Tiwas TTRPG Systems Readiness Auditor and Adaptation Analyst  
**Adventure source:** *Beyond the Vale of Madness — GURPS*, v1.2, supplied parsed PDF text/images  
**Tiwas source:** *Tiwas — Alpha-Playtest Corpus (One-Off, GM Table-Ready)*, 2026-09-01  
**Audit posture:** Mechanical readiness benchmark, not a conversion document

---

# 1. Executive Summary

## 1.1 Overall Finding

**The adventure is not currently fully playtestable in Tiwas.**

Tiwas can already support the **core transactional act of making a roll-under d100 Skill test**, including resource cost, Overflow, Failure XP, Recovery, and Advanced Skill triggers. Therefore, many of the adventure’s ordinary GURPS skill and attribute rolls can be mechanically represented as **Tiwas Core Tests**, provided adventure-specific Tiwas skill mappings are authored.

However, the adventure makes heavy use of systems that are either **missing**, **only partially ruled**, or **not content-complete** in the current Tiwas baseline:

* combat attack/damage resolution;
* weapon damage and damage types;
* monster stat blocks and creature templates;
* tactical movement / map combat / reach / turn sequencing;
* armor and shield interaction with damage;
* fall damage and environmental hazards;
* fatigue / exhaustion / hypothermia;
* grappling and ongoing corrosive absorption;
* fright/fear consequences;
* equipment, encumbrance, carrying capacity, and item stats;
* magic, enchantment, powers, and GURPS-style advantages;
* healing amounts and immediate First Aid outcomes;
* economy / loot conversion / advancement reward mapping.

The adventure is therefore useful as a **diagnostic benchmark**: it exposes that Tiwas’ Core Test architecture is mature enough for binary task checks, but the surrounding adventure-facing subsystems required by a fantasy dungeon/survival scenario are not yet sufficiently complete for a full adventure playtest.

## 1.2 Positive Readiness

The following Tiwas functions are **Playtestable Now**, subject to adaptation mapping where noted:

| Function | Tiwas readiness |
|---|---|
| d100 roll-under task resolution | **Playtestable Now** — Canonical / Locked Core Test |
| failure XP and advancement from failed rolls | **Playtestable Now** — Canonical / Locked |
| resource cost and Overflow | **Playtestable Now** — Canonical / Locked |
| ordinary binary task checks | **Adaptation Mapping Required** — underlying Core Test exists |
| opposed contests | **Playtestable Now** for primitive; **Adaptation Mapping Required** for skills/NPC values |
| HP = 0 incapacitation | **Playtestable Now** as Non-canonical designer ruling |
| paragraph state flags / adventure variables | **Adventure Content Only** |
| General XP awards | **Playtestable Now** as Core economy; reward conversion required |

## 1.3 Critical Blockers

| Critical blocker | Responsible Tiwas area | Why it blocks the adventure |
|---|---|---|
| No complete combat loop | S-1/S-3/S-4/S-5/S-6/S-7/S-12 plus missing attack/damage content | Ice troll and blood man encounters require attacks, defenses, damage, tactics, monster stats, retreat, and death/incapacitation. |
| No non-Overflow damage magnitude system | S-3/S-4 incomplete for damage magnitude | Adventure uses explicit damage dice for weapons, falls, traps, claws, corrosive seep, and hypothermia. Tiwas has HP and Overflow but no general mapped damage amounts. |
| No creature stat blocks/templates | S-12 Open / content not table-ready | Ice troll and blood man require Tiwas attributes, skills, HP, defenses, attacks, traits, and special abilities. |
| Equipment and weapons not established | Reserved / missing subsystem, S-5 partial armor only | Adventure depends on swords, mace, dagger, crossbow, armor, shield, rope, pitons, torches, lockpicking with dagger, item weight, ST requirements, and encumbrance. |
| Environmental hazard model absent | Reserved / missing subsystem; S-2 notes systemic hazards but no mechanics | Cold, hypothermia, falls, icy stairs, cliffs, snow digging, and darkness are mechanically active. |
| Fatigue/exhaustion not available | Missing subsystem / no separate fatigue economy | Adventure repeatedly subtracts FP and uses FP = 0 collapse/death. Tiwas has Physical Energy but no fixed attritional fatigue system. |
| Magic/special abilities absent | Reserved / missing subsystem | Pregenerated spellcaster, enchanted dagger, powerstone, Night Vision, Fearlessness, Luck, Regeneration, Regrowth, Injury Tolerance, etc. are not supported as Tiwas mechanics. |

## 1.4 Best Immediate Use of the Adventure

The adventure is suitable now for a **limited alpha diagnostic**, not a full playtest:

1. Use it to test **ordinary Core Tests** for noncombat choices.
2. Use it to test **resource cost, Overflow, Failure XP, and Recovery** during exploration checks.
3. Use it to identify where Tiwas needs formal subsystem completion before fantasy adventure play.
4. Do **not** use it yet as a full Tiwas combat/adventure validation scenario.

---

# 2. Audit Objective and Method

## 2.1 Objective

The objective is to use *Beyond the Vale of Madness — GURPS* as an external practical benchmark for Tiwas readiness.

The audit asks:

> What mechanical functions does the adventure require, and can Tiwas currently perform those functions using the current Tiwas baseline?

This audit does **not** attempt to preserve GURPS procedures. GURPS is treated only as the source adventure’s expression of mechanical demand.

## 2.2 Method

The audit followed this procedure:

1. Identify every meaningful mechanical requirement in the adventure text.
2. Convert ordinary GURPS attribute/skill rolls into the requirement:  
   **“perform a standard Tiwas Core Test.”**
3. Classify each requirement against the Tiwas baseline:
   * Canonical / Locked;
   * Non-canonical designer ruling;
   * Design-stage / Open;
   * Missing;
   * Adventure content only.
4. Determine whether the requirement is:
   * Playtestable Now;
   * Adaptation Mapping Required;
   * Design-Stage Dependency;
   * Missing Subsystem;
   * Adventure Content Only.
5. Identify whether each gap blocks:
   * full adventure playtesting;
   * only specific optional branches;
   * only exact conversion fidelity;
   * only campaign/economy follow-up.

## 2.3 Important Interpretive Constraint

All ordinary GURPS skill rolls and attribute rolls are treated as requiring the **standard Tiwas Core Test**.

Therefore:

* GURPS `DX roll`, `ST roll`, `Will roll`, `Merchant roll`, etc. are **not** imported as GURPS mechanics.
* Each such roll must be mapped to an appropriate Tiwas Skill.
* The Tiwas Core Test transaction remains intact:
  1. Roll d100.
  2. Determine resource domain.
  3. Determine success/failure.
  4. Pay Cost equal to natural roll.
  5. Apply Overflow if needed.
  6. Resolve Failure XP.
  7. Resolve failed Double / Advanced Skill effects.
  8. Recover resource.
  9. End test.

## 2.4 Status Caveat

The supplied Tiwas Alpha-Playtest Corpus is itself explicitly **not canonical** and does not promote any rule. It compiles:

* Canonical / Locked rules;
* Non-canonical designer rulings;
* Open or non-table-ready items.

This audit respects the status labels in that corpus.

---

# 3. Source Adventure Mechanical Inventory

This section records the adventure’s mechanical demands before assessing Tiwas compatibility.

## 3.1 Navigation, State, and Solo-Adventure Procedure

| Requirement | Adventure use |
|---|---|
| Choose-your-path paragraph navigation | Entire adventure, especially #1 and all numbered transitions |
| Inventory notation | “As you find any items … jot that down,” About the Adventure |
| State flags | `DARKNESS` at #7; `AMBUSHED` at #20; `RESCUER` at #32 / #60 |
| Conditional endings | Death/unconscious endings at #15, #17, #38, #52; successful return at #60 |

# 4. System-by-System Tiwas Compatibility Assessment

## 4.1 Core d100 Resolution and Ordinary Tests

| Adventure requirement | Where used | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Readiness | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Resolve ordinary skill/attribute checks | Will, DX, ST, Climbing, Search, Merchant, Tracking, etc. | Tiwas Core Test resolves roll-under Skill tests with d100, cost, Overflow, XP, Recovery | Canonical / Locked: DEC-001–DEC-012 | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Major but tractable | Author Tiwas skill mapping for each adventure test. Attribute-only GURPS rolls cannot be rolled directly as GURPS attributes; they need Tiwas Skill mappings. |
| Preserve resource cost on every test | Every Core Test adaptation | Cost equals natural roll; PE or MP depending on skill domain | Canonical / Locked: DEC-006/007 | **Playtestable Now** | Systemically important | Must decide whether each mapped skill is Body- or Mind-rooted. |
| Handle failed rolls and advancement | Any failed check | Failure XP, Skill Roll Pool, General XP, Advanced Skill creation | Canonical / Locked: DEC-009–DEC-012 | **Playtestable Now** | Positive readiness | No adventure-specific blocker, but playtest logs should record XP effects. |
| Handle GURPS unskilled defaults | DX-5, IQ-4, ST-4, etc. | Tiwas has Skill starting values and difficulty modifiers, but no GURPS default conversion | Core skill architecture Canonical; difficulty Non-canonical; exact mapping absent | **Adaptation Mapping Required / Design-Stage Dependency** | Major | Need policy for untrained attempts: existing Tier-1 skill, authored Advanced Skill, zero skill, or difficulty penalty. |

### Assessment

The **Core Test transaction itself is ready**. The adventure’s many binary exploration checks can exercise it immediately once a Tiwas adaptation author decides which Tiwas Skill each check uses.

However, Tiwas does not currently provide a complete canonical skill dictionary matching adventure activities like Lockpicking, Climbing, Survival, Physician, or Tactics. That is not a failure of the Core Test, but it is an adaptation-content requirement.

---

## 4.2 Difficulty, Modifiers, and Defaults

| Adventure requirement | Where used | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Readiness | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Easier/harder task modifiers | #18 +2, #27 +3, #35 -3, #58 -2, etc. | S-8 establishes named difficulty tiers with fixed additive Skill-side modifiers | Non-canonical designer ruling: DEC-063–DEC-066 | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Major | Supplied corpus does not provide the actual fixed modifier table. Cannot consistently map GURPS numeric modifiers. |
| Apply modifier to success and XP | All modified checks | Effective Skill used for success, Failure XP, and Skill Roll Pool cascade entry | Non-canonical: DEC-064/065 | **Playtestable Now in architecture; not complete in values** | Moderate | Needs numeric grade values and adventure-specific difficulty mapping. |
| Encumbrance penalty to Climbing | #15 | Tiwas encumbrance is Reserved / not defined | Reserved by DEC-015 | **Missing Subsystem** | Moderate | Need encumbrance/load subsystem or adventure-specific substitute. |
| Darkness attack penalty | #38 | Difficulty can modify Skill side, but attack/darkness combat interaction not defined | S-8 partial; combat missing | **Design-Stage Dependency / Missing Combat Dependency** | Major in blood man fight | Need darkness/visibility condition and combat attack mapping. |

### Assessment

S-8 gives Tiwas the **shape** of a difficulty system but not enough supplied mechanical detail to execute all adventure modifiers. The adventure is modifier-heavy, so a full playtest needs S-8’s fixed modifier table and a conversion policy.

## 4.3 Opposed Contests

| Adventure requirement | Where used | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Readiness | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sneak past ice troll | #44 Quick Contest of Stealth vs Perception 12 | S-1 Universal Opposed Contest | Canonical / Locked: DEC-013 | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Major for cave path | Need Tiwas Stealth-equivalent Skill, troll Perception-equivalent Skill/stat, and Quality mode selection. |
| Mutual success tie-breaking | Any opposed contest | S-1 Quality comparison by Margin/Blackjack/Hybrid | Canonical / Locked | **Playtestable Now** | Low/moderate | Need select Quality mode; likely Margin for stealth/precision. |
| Mutual failure | Any opposed contest | Repeat contest; third-party adjudication exists if relevant | S-1 Canonical; S-8 DEC-043 non-canonical for third-party adjudication | **Playtestable Now** | Low | #44 can use repeat-on-mutual-failure without third party. |
| Combat opposition | #17, #38 | S-1 can be primitive for opposed actions, but complete attack/defense/effect/magnitude loop absent | Partial: S-1/S-3/S-6 | **Design-Stage Dependency / Missing Subsystem** | Critical | Need combat procedure, NPC stats, damage/effect magnitude, equipment, defense mitigation. |

### Assessment

The opposed-contest primitive is ready. The adventure’s **stealth contest** is a good candidate for immediate S-1 testing once NPC values are authored. Combat cannot be made ready merely by invoking S-1 because the downstream combat payload is not complete.

## 4.4 S-2 Location Index and Hit/Impact Location

| Adventure requirement | Where used | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Readiness | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Determine location for attacks/effects | Armor coverage, Blood Seep large-area injury, possible wounds | Zero-Step Tier-1 Location Index provider exists | Canonical / Locked: DEC-014 | **Partial / Design-Stage Dependency** | Major for armor/wounds | Zero-Step gives a number, but the full anatomical mapping and exact ranges are not fully supplied in executable form. |
| Non-attack physical hazards produce location | Falls, traps, environmental injury | DEC-037 governs failed-roll provenance for non-attack Location Index | Non-canonical designer ruling | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Moderate | Only matters if the adapted hazard uses location-referencing Effects. |
| Systemic hazards need no location | Extreme temperature, poison-like hazards | DEC-037 exempts systemic threats such as Extreme Temperature | Non-canonical designer ruling | **Playtestable as principle; mechanics missing** | Major for cold | Direct HP/conditions are allowed, but actual cold/hypothermia mechanics are absent. |
| Armor location check at Tier 0 | Armor coverage | S-5 uses single-purpose Zero-Step read for armor coverage | Non-canonical DEC-062 | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Major for combat/falls | Needs armor tags, coverage templates, and damage/effect interaction. |

### Assessment

Tiwas has an elegant **Location Index provider**, but the adventure requires more than a number. It needs anatomical mapping, armor coverage, injury consequences, and creature templates. Those remain incomplete or content-dependent.

| Force retreat / compel yield | Troll may retreat at #17 | Open Retreat / Compel Yield is base-tier Effect | Non-canonical DEC-023 | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Moderate | Troll retreat is adventure-authored morale behavior, not necessarily S-3 Effect use. |

| Powerstone energy | Enfys | No Tiwas powerstone/magic-energy subsystem | Missing | **Missing Subsystem** | Major if spellcaster used | Need resource interaction policy preserving Core invariants. |
| Enchanted Shatterproof dagger | #24 | No enchantment/item property subsystem | Missing / equipment Tags possible but not authored | **Missing Subsystem** | Low/moderate | Need item Tag/effect definition. |
| Night Vision | #38, Enfys spell list, blood man trait | No vision trait/effect subsystem | Missing / Condition tier open | **Missing Subsystem** | Major in blood man fight if darkness occurs | Need visibility and sensory trait rules. |
| Regeneration / Regrowth | Ice troll | No special ability subsystem | Missing | **Missing Subsystem** | Major in troll fight fidelity | Need regeneration timing and environmental condition interaction. |
| Luck, Fit, Charisma, Magery, racial traits, disadvantages | Pregens | No full trait/advantage/disadvantage implementation | Missing | **Missing Subsystem** | Major for using pregens faithfully | Need Tiwas character trait system. |

### Assessment

The adventure’s supplied spellcaster and many monster/character traits are not currently supported.

## 4.18 Economy, Treasure, and Advancement Rewards

| Adventure requirement | Where used | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Readiness | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Track loot items | Throughout; treasure table | Inventory notation can be narrative/adventure content | Adventure Content Only | **Playtestable Now** | Low | No system needed to write down items. |
| Monetary values | Treasure table, #60 | Tiwas economy/equipment reserved | Reserved DEC-015 | **Adventure Content Only / Missing Economy** | Moderate | Need Tiwas currency/economy if mechanically relevant. |
| Loot threshold >$500 | #60 | Can be checked as adventure condition if using source values | Adventure Content Only | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Low/moderate | Decide whether GURPS dollars map directly, abstractly, or not at all. |
| Character-point awards | #60 | Tiwas has General XP | Canonical DEC-011 | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Moderate | Need conversion from adventure “character points” to Tiwas General XP. |
| Reward for rescue | #60 | Can be narrative/inventory content | Adventure Content Only | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Low | Need currency mapping if economy matters. |

### Assessment

Treasure tracking is easy; economy and advancement conversion are not established. This does not block short-form diagnostic play, but it does block campaign-continuity play.

# 5. Playtestability Matrix

## 5.1 Classification Key

| Classification | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Playtestable Now** | Tiwas currently provides sufficient mechanics. |
| **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Tiwas has the underlying mechanic, but adventure-specific mapping/content must be authored. |
| **Design-Stage Dependency** | Tiwas has a ruling direction or partial subsystem, but not enough executable detail for dependable play. |
| **Missing Subsystem** | No adequate Tiwas mechanism currently exists. |
| **Adventure Content Only** | Setting, pathing, item identity, NPC name, treasure list, etc.; not a Tiwas mechanical gap. |

## 5.2 Matrix by Tiwas System

| Tiwas area | Adventure exercises it? | Readiness | Blocking significance | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Core d100 / Core Test | Yes, heavily | **Playtestable Now** | Positive foundation | All ordinary rolls become Core Tests. |
| Skill mapping | Yes | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Major | Need Tiwas skills for Climbing, Lockpicking, Survival, Search, etc. |
| Resource Cost / Overflow | Yes, every test | **Playtestable Now** | Positive foundation | Must be preserved; may make exploration checks dangerous. |
| Failure XP / Advanced Skills | Yes, indirectly | **Playtestable Now** | Low/positive | Adventure can stress advancement during failed checks. |
| S-1 Opposed Contest | Yes, #44 and combat conceptually | **Playtestable Now / Adaptation Mapping Required** | Moderate | Stealth contest can work once NPC values exist. |
| S-2 Location Index | Yes, via armor/injury needs | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Major | Zero-Step exists; anatomical mapping/content incomplete. |
| S-3 Effects | Yes, combat/conditions | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Critical | Effect structure exists; damage/condition payloads incomplete. |
| S-4 Injury/Wounds | Yes | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Critical | HP exists; wound consequences and damage magnitude absent. |
| S-5 Armor | Yes | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Major/critical | Tags-only armor direction conflicts with direct DR import; content absent. |
| S-6 Defense | Yes | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Critical | Defense architecture exists; mitigation/equipment/combat details absent. |
| S-7 Incapacitation/Death | Yes | **Playtestable Now / Partial** | Moderate | HP=0 incap works; adventure instant death alignment unresolved. |
| S-8 Difficulty | Yes, heavily | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Major | Fixed modifier table not supplied. |
| S-9/S-10 Extended Tests | Lightly | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Low/moderate | Useful for digging/healing if designer chooses. |
| S-11 Healing | Yes | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Major | Immediate First Aid HP restoration not ready. |
| S-12 Creatures | Yes, critically | **Missing Content / Design-Stage Dependency** | Critical | Ice troll and blood man not available as Tiwas creatures. |
| Equipment/weapons | Yes, heavily | **Missing Subsystem** | Critical | Needed for almost every combat/exploration branch. |
| Encumbrance/load | Yes | **Missing Subsystem** | Moderate | Climbing and treasure carry use it. |
| Environmental hazards | Yes, heavily | **Missing Subsystem** | Critical/major | Cold, falls, darkness, hypothermia, exhaustion. |
| Fatigue/exhaustion | Yes | **Missing Subsystem** | Critical/major | Adventure uses FP loss and FP=0 collapse. |
| Magic/special abilities | Yes, if pregens used | **Missing Subsystem** | Major/critical | Enfys and monster traits depend on it. |
| Economy/loot | Yes | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Low/moderate | Can track source values but Tiwas economy not established. |
| Advancement rewards | Yes | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Moderate | Need character-point to General XP mapping. |

These are not necessarily Tiwas system gaps, but must be authored before play:

# 7. Adventure Path Dependency Analysis

## 7.1 High-Level Path Map

| Path / branch | Key paragraphs | Main mechanical dependencies | Readiness |

| Courtyard and guardhouse | #3, #43, #2, #11, #18, #40, #30, #13, #6 | Search, Will, Lockpicking, Forced Entry, loot, shield | **Exploration tests testable; equipment/loot mapping needed** |

## 7.2 Shortest Low-Combat Diagnostic Route

A designer could construct a limited diagnostic route that avoids full combat, for example:

`#1 → #19 → #3 → #43 → #14 → #33 → #23 → #55 → #46 → #53 → #60`

This still exercises:

* Survival / cold;
* Search;
* Merchant;
* DX jump;
* corrosive injury;
* loot tracking;
* reward/ending.

Even this route is **not fully supported** because it includes environmental damage, possible FP/hypothermia, jump/fall damage, and corrosive damage.

## 7.3 Combat-Heavy Diagnostic Route

The troll route:

`#1 → #12 → #9 → #31 → #8/#41 → #44/#17 → #21`

This route stresses:

* stealth opposed contest;
* monster detection;
* tactical combat;
* attacks and defenses;
* monster morale;
* HP damage;
* regeneration/natural DR;
* healing;
* FP cost from digging.

This route is currently **blocked at multiple critical layers**.

## 7.4 Blood Man Route

The blood man route:

`#33 → #55 → #7/#46 → #38 → #48 → #56/#60`

This route stresses:

* darkness and light source handling;
* Fright Checks;
* tactical positioning via Tactics;
* attack penalty from darkness;
* grappling;
* corrosive ongoing damage;
* Injury Tolerance / Night Vision;
* Will to search gore;
* treasure and ending.

This is the single densest subsystem stress test in the adventure and is **not currently Tiwas-playtestable** except as a gap demonstration.

---

# 8. Tiwas Readiness Assessment

## 8.1 Full Adventure Readiness

**Classification:** **Not Ready for Full Tiwas Playtest**

Reason:

The adventure’s complete mechanical envelope requires multiple systems that Tiwas does not yet provide in executable form. The Core Test is ready, but the adventure is not merely a sequence of binary checks. It is a fantasy survival/combat scenario with equipment, monsters, hazards, damage, and magic.

## 8.2 Partial Diagnostic Readiness

**Classification:** **Partially Playtestable as an Alpha Diagnostic**

Tiwas can currently test:

* Core Test transaction under repeated exploration checks;
* resource-domain selection pressure;
* Overflow consequences from tests;
* Failure XP and skill advancement;
* simple branch-state recording;
* S-1 opposed contest primitive in stealth, if NPC values are authored;
* HP = 0 incapacitation once damage exists or is manually assigned for test purposes.

However, such a session must be explicitly labeled as a **partial diagnostic**, not a full adventure conversion.

## 8.3 Canonical Readiness vs Non-Canonical Readiness

| Layer | Readiness |
|---|---|
| Canonical Core | Strong for task resolution; insufficient alone for adventure play |
| Non-canonical subsystems | Several directions exist, but many are partial or content-incomplete |
| Open / missing systems | Numerous critical blockers for fantasy adventure play |

## 8.4 Systems the Adventure Does *Not* Strongly Require

The adventure does **not** materially require:

| System | Reason |
|---|---|
| Third-party adjudication | No meaningful third-party contest arbitration appears. |
| Deep campaign procedure | Adventure is a solo one-shot. |
| Social influence system | Social rewards are branch outcomes, not negotiated mechanically. |
| Crafting | Not used. |
| Large-scale travel rules beyond cold Survival | Travel is mostly narrative except #19. |
| Complex rest scheduling | Healing appears as immediate First Aid, not long rest management. |

---

# 9. Development Priorities Exposed by the Adventure

## Priority 1 — Combat Payload and Damage Magnitude

**Responsible systems:** S-3, S-4, S-6, S-7, equipment, S-12

Tiwas needs a complete way to answer:

* When an attack succeeds, what happens?
* How much HP damage occurs?
* How are weapon Tags or creature attacks expressed?
* How does armor reduce, redirect, block, or alter the effect?
* How does Active Defense mitigate an already-applied Effect?
* How do multiple attacks/effects per turn work?

Without this, neither the ice troll nor blood man can be run.

## Priority 2 — Creature / NPC Content Authoring

**Responsible system:** S-12

The adventure requires at least:

* Ice Troll;
* Blood Man;
* injured hunter as noncombat NPC;
* optional implied tundra wolves/grave ghouls only if expanded.

Tiwas needs a table-ready creature stat-block format and content authoring standard.

## Priority 3 — Equipment, Weapons, Armor, and Shields

**Responsible systems:** Equipment subsystem, S-5, S-6

The adventure exposes the need for:

* weapon Tags and attack profiles;
* shields as defensive equipment;
* armor coverage Tags;
* tool permissions and bonuses;
* item weight/load interaction;
* weapon prerequisites or equivalents;
* light sources.

The S-5 Tags-only armor ruling is directionally useful but insufficient by itself.

## Priority 4 — Environmental Hazards and Fatigue

**Responsible systems:** Environmental hazards, Conditions, possible fatigue-as-Condition policy

Needed for:

* extreme cold;
* hypothermia;
* fixed exertion costs;
* falls;
* slippery terrain;
* darkness;
* wind gusts;
* collapse from exhaustion.

This adventure is an excellent benchmark for whether Tiwas can support survival exploration.

## Priority 5 — Difficulty Table and Skill Mapping Policy

**Responsible system:** S-8 plus skill taxonomy/adaptation guidance

The adventure has many numeric GURPS modifiers and unskilled defaults. Tiwas needs:

* fixed named difficulty modifier values;
* a policy for converting adventure difficulty statements;
* a policy for untrained attempts;
* recommended mapping from common fantasy tasks to Tiwas Skills.

## Priority 6 — Healing and First Aid

**Responsible system:** S-11

Needed for:

* post-combat bandaging;
* immediate HP restoration;
* stabilizing/rescuing injured NPCs;
* possible spell healing if magic is added.

S-11’s Extended Test framing is useful but does not yet satisfy the adventure’s immediate First Aid use.

## Priority 7 — Conditions: Darkness, Fear, Grappled, Wounded, Hypothermia

**Responsible systems:** S-3 Condition tier, S-4, environmental hazards, combat

The blood man encounter especially requires concrete condition handling.

## Priority 8 — Magic and Special Traits

**Responsible systems:** Magic/special abilities, creature traits, item enchantments

Not needed for every route, but necessary if using the supplied Enfys character or preserving monster traits.

## Priority 9 — Economy and Advancement Mapping

**Responsible systems:** Economy/equipment; General XP reward policy

Needed for campaign carry-forward, not for immediate mechanical survival.

---

# 10. Conclusions

## 10.1 Primary Conclusion

*Beyond the Vale of Madness — GURPS* is an effective Tiwas readiness benchmark because it immediately exposes the boundary between Tiwas’ strong Core Test architecture and its incomplete adventure-facing subsystems.

The Core is ready. The adventure is not.

## 10.2 What Can Be Playtested Now

Tiwas can currently playtest:

* ordinary exploration checks as Core Tests;
* success/failure branching;
* resource cost and Overflow from tests;
* Failure XP and Advanced Skill creation;
* simple opposed contests;
* state flags as adventure content;
* HP = 0 incapacitation once damage is available.

## 10.3 What Cannot Be Fully Playtested

Tiwas cannot yet fully playtest:

* the ice troll encounter;
* the blood man encounter;
* weapon damage;
* armor/DR interactions;
* falling and environmental damage;
* fatigue loss and collapse;
* Fright Check consequences;
* grappling and corrosive seep;
* magic/spellcasting;
* pregenerated GURPS characters as mechanical equivalents;
* treasure economy and character-point reward conversion.

## 10.4 Diagnostic Value

The adventure strongly suggests that Tiwas’ next development phase should focus on:

1. combat/damage/effect payloads;
2. equipment/weapons/armor;
3. creature stat blocks;
4. environmental hazards/fatigue;
5. difficulty values and common skill mapping;
6. healing and conditions.

Until those are complete, the adventure should be used as a **requirements checklist**, not as a full conversion target.

---

# 12. Explicit Assumptions / Unresolved Questions

## 12.1 Assumptions Made

1. **Ordinary GURPS rolls become Tiwas Core Tests.**  
   No GURPS roll-under, 3d6, Quick Contest, Fright Check, or default mechanic is imported.

2. **A Tiwas “attribute roll” requires a Skill mapping.**  
   The supplied Tiwas Core defines Skill tests. Therefore GURPS DX/ST/IQ/Will rolls must be mapped to appropriate Tiwas Skills rather than rolled directly as GURPS attributes.

3. **Adventure damage expressions are requirements, not usable Tiwas mechanics.**  
   Damage such as `1d-3 cut` or `1d+2 cut` indicates that the adventure needs a damage system. It is not automatically imported into Tiwas.

4. **State words such as `DARKNESS`, `AMBUSHED`, and `RESCUER` are adventure content unless their effects require Tiwas mechanics.**

5. **The supplied Tiwas corpus is used as the status baseline.**  
   Where it says material is non-canonical or open, this audit treats it accordingly.

6. **The source wording “gain 2 characters” at #60 is not corrected silently.**  
   It appears to mean “gain 2 character points,” but the audit treats that as unresolved source wording.

## 12.2 Unresolved Questions for Tiwa

| Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| What are the fixed numeric S-8 difficulty modifiers? | Required for nearly every modified adventure test. |
| How should common fantasy tasks map to Tiwas Skills? | Required for Climbing, Survival, Lockpicking, First Aid, Merchant, Search, Tactics, etc. |
| How does Tiwas assign HP damage from a successful attack or hazard? | Critical blocker for combat and environmental play. |
| How does Active Defense mitigate an applied Effect numerically or categorically? | S-6 architecture exists but adventure combat needs concrete output. |
| Are fatigue/exhaustion effects modeled as PE loss, HP damage, Conditions, or something else? | Adventure uses FP loss and FP = 0 collapse. |
| How should falls and hypothermia be represented? | Frequent exploration hazards. |
| What is the table-ready creature stat-block format? | Needed for ice troll and blood man. |
| How are weapons represented? | Needed for every combat-capable character and treasure weapon. |
| How are shields represented? | Needed for medium shield and Block-like defense. |
| How should immediate First Aid healing work? | Adventure restores HP immediately after troll fight. |
| Will Tiwas have a fear/fright condition system? | Required by #38 and #58. |
| How are magic, enchantments, and powers intended to integrate with the Core Test resource economy? | Required for Enfys and enchanted items. |
| Should adventure loot values map directly to Tiwas economy, or become abstract treasure ratings? | Needed for #60 reward and loot threshold. |
| What General XP amount corresponds to the adventure’s character-point award? | Needed for advancement. |

## 12.3 Final Audit Statement

The adventure is an excellent benchmark for Tiwas because it demands a complete fantasy-adventure mechanical stack. Current Tiwas can support the **roll transaction layer**, but not yet the full **adventure execution layer**.

**Recommended next action:** complete a minimal fantasy-adventure readiness slice consisting of:

1. task skill mapping + S-8 numeric difficulty values;
2. basic combat attack/effect/damage loop;
3. weapon/armor/shield Tags and payloads;
4. two creature templates: Ice Troll and Blood Man;
5. fall/cold/darkness/fatigue hazard rules;
6. immediate First Aid / healing rule;
7. reward conversion to General XP.

Only after that slice exists should *Beyond the Vale of Madness* be attempted as a full Tiwas playtest.

```markdown
# Tiwas TTRPG — *Beyond the Vale of Madness* Adaptation Readiness Audit

# 1. Executive Summary

## 1.1 Finding

**Beyond the Vale of Madness is an excellent readiness benchmark for Tiwas because it is mechanically small but touches a surprisingly broad cross-section of RPG subsystems.**

The adventure contains:

* ordinary skill/attribute tests;
* difficulty modifiers;
* opposed contests;
* combat;
* attacks and defensive resolution;
* damage;
* HP;
* armour/DR;
* grappling;
* tactical positioning;
* falling and environmental hazards;
* fatigue/exhaustion;
* healing;
* incapacitation/death;
* fear/fright;
* equipment;
* encumbrance/carrying;
* weapons;
* ranged weapons;
* special abilities;
* magic;
* NPC/creature construction;
* creature regeneration;
* conditions/status-like effects;
* time/duration;
* rewards/economy;
* character advancement;
* adventure-state tracking.

That makes it substantially more useful than an adventure containing only generic skill checks.

### Overall readiness conclusion

**Tiwas cannot currently run the entire adventure as a clean, mechanically complete Tiwas playtest without adaptation work.**

However, the result is **much better than the historical Canonical v2.1 status would suggest**, because the 1 September Alpha corpus contains a large set of subsequently ruled non-canonical subsystems.

In particular, the following are now sufficiently specified for alpha table use:

* Core Test;
* S-1 opposed contests;
* S-2 Zero-Step/location framework;
* S-3 base Effect architecture;
* S-4 injury/wound direction;
* S-5 armour direction;
* S-6 active defence;
* S-7 incapacitation/death direction;
* S-8 difficulty;
* S-9/S-10 Extended Tests;
* S-11 Rest/healing.

The Alpha corpus explicitly describes itself as a one-off table-ready assembly of currently Locked and Ruled material, while retaining the distinction that the ruled material is **non-canonical**. 

Therefore the benchmark is now showing something important:

> **The remaining problem is no longer simply “Tiwas lacks many RPG subsystems.” It is that some systems are mechanically ruled but still lack complete content, implementation, or adaptation interfaces.**

---

# 2. Audit Objective and Method

## 2.1 Benchmark principle

The adventure is being treated as a **black-box requirements test**.

The question is not:

> “How do we translate GURPS?”

The question is:

> **“If this adventure were handed to a Tiwas GM today, what rules would the GM need in order to resolve every mechanical situation presented by the adventure?”**

This is the correct benchmark because the adventure is already a functioning published scenario.

The adventure itself describes *The Castle of Madness* as an introductory solo adventure for GURPS Fantasy/Dungeon Fantasy and provides two pregenerated characters. 

---

# 3. Source Adventure Mechanical Inventory

## 3.1 Core mechanical requirements identified

|  # | Adventure system requirement   | Evidence in adventure                                                                  | Tiwas requirement                      |
| -: | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
|  1 | Ordinary skill tests           | DX, Will, Search, Survival, Climbing, Lockpicking, Merchant, Tracking, First Aid, etc. | Core Test                              |
|  2 | Attribute-based fallback tests | DX-5, ST-4, IQ-4, etc.                                                                 | Core Test with Tiwas task mapping      |
|  3 | Test modifiers                 | +2, +3, -2, -3, -5, -8, etc.                                                           | Difficulty / Skill-side modification   |
|  4 | Opposed contest                | Stealth vs Perception                                                                  | S-1                                    |
|  5 | Combat                         | Ice troll and Blood Man encounters                                                     | Combat architecture                    |
|  6 | Attack resolution              | Claws, maw, weapons                                                                    | Combat + S-3                           |
|  7 | Defence                        | Dodge, Parry; explicit All-Out Attack/no defence                                       | S-6                                    |

# 4. System-by-System Compatibility Assessment

## 4.1 Ordinary Skill Resolution

### Adventure requirement

The adventure repeatedly instructs the player to make a named skill roll.

Examples include:

* Will;
* DX;
* Climbing;
* Survival;
* Search;
* Lockpicking;
* Tracking;
* First Aid;
* Physician;
* Merchant;
* Stealth;
* Tactics.

The adventure also supplies attribute-based fallbacks when the relevant skill is absent. For example, Lockpicking becomes DX-3 and Search becomes Perception-5. 

### Tiwas status

**Playtestable Now — Core Resolution**

Every such test can use the Tiwas Core Test.

The canonical transaction already establishes:

1. roll;
2. determine resource domain;
3. success/failure;
4. pay natural-roll cost;
5. resolve Overflow;
6. resolve Failure XP;
7. resolve failed Double;
8. recover;
9. end test.



### Important limitation

The **resolution engine is ready**.

The **adventure-to-Tiwas skill taxonomy is not automatically solved**.

This is an adaptation-content problem rather than evidence that the Core Test is missing.

**Readiness: 🟢 Playtestable Now, with adaptation mapping.**

---

# 5. Difficulty Modifiers

The adventure uses explicit numerical modifiers such as:

* +2 Lockpicking;
* +3 Tracking;
* -2 Fright Check;
* -3 Climbing;
* -5 Search;
* -8 climbing fallback;
* encumbrance penalties.

Tiwas now has a ruled S-8 architecture in which difficulty modifies **effective Skill**, never the natural die. The effective Skill is used for success/failure, Failure XP and the Skill Roll Pool cascade. Grades are symmetric. 

### Result

The *function* is available.

What remains is the **actual Tiwas difficulty-grade numerical table/interface** needed to translate the adventure's explicit GURPS modifiers.

Therefore:

**Readiness: 🟡 Adaptation Mapping Required**

This does **not** require importing GURPS's difficulty system.

---

# 6. Opposed Tests

The adventure explicitly uses a Quick Contest:

> Stealth vs distracted creature's Perception 12.



Tiwas S-1 is directly applicable.

S-1 independently resolves both participants' Core Tests and uses the success/failure matrix, with Quality resolving success/success outcomes. 

### Result

The adventure's Stealth-vs-Perception situation is a very strong direct test of S-1.

**Readiness: 🟢 Playtestable Now**

This is one of the clearest successes of the benchmark.

---

# 7. Combat

## 7.1 Requirement

The adventure contains two explicit combat encounters.

The ice troll encounter allows either abstract combat or tactical combat using the supplied map. 

The Blood Man encounter likewise supports tactical combat and specifies attacks, grappling, damage and special abilities. 

## 7.2 Tiwas status

This is the largest remaining integration problem.

Although S-1, S-3, S-5 and S-6 now have ruled architectures, **the complete Combat subsystem is not equivalent to having those individual rulings**.

The Alpha corpus provides:

* Effect application;
* Active Defense;
* armour interaction;
* injury/wound architecture.

But the complete combat procedure still needs a coherent operational interface for:

* declaring attacks;
* determining the appropriate attacking Skill;
* tactical sequencing;
* movement;
* range;
* weapon interaction;
* combat timing;
* grappling;
* ongoing combat effects.

### Result

**Readiness: 🔴 Design-Stage / Integration Dependency**

Combat is therefore the **primary benchmark blocker**.

---

# 8. Damage and Harm

The adventure contains numerous explicit damage events:

* falling;
* weapon attacks;
* claws;
* maw;
* corrosive Blood Seep;
* environmental injury.

For example, failed climbing can produce `2d-2` crushing damage, while the Blood Man's Blood Seep produces ongoing corrosive damage. 

Tiwas now has the important architectural distinction:

* **Injury = HP damage**
* **Wound = localized lasting numerical state.**

The S-4 ruling explicitly separates those tracks. 

However, the exact adaptation of GURPS damage dice/types to Tiwas's Effect architecture is not established by the adventure audit.

### Result

**Readiness: 🟡 Design-stage integration**

The underlying Tiwas harm architecture exists substantially, but the complete operational damage model required by combat and hazards is not demonstrated by the available table-ready corpus.

---

# 9. Armour

The adventure explicitly uses armour and DR.

The Blood Man has DR 1 and the Ice Troll DR 2. The pregenerated characters have location-specific armour such as torso, arms, hands and feet protection. 

Tiwas S-5 now has a ruled armour architecture:

* Armor Tags;
* location-bound protection;
* shared individual-creature anatomy;
* Zero-Step support for Tier-0 armour checks;
* Armor Bypass and Sunder interactions.



### Result

The **architecture is substantially ready for alpha use**, but the adventure still requires actual Tiwas armour items/tags.

**Readiness: 🟡 Adaptation Mapping / Content**

---

# 10. Hit Location

This adventure provides a particularly useful hit-location test because armour coverage is explicitly anatomical.

Tiwas now has Zero-Step as the canonical Tier-1 numeric provider, but the current corpus makes clear that location is not simply synonymous with the entire hit-location subsystem. 

The Alpha corpus subsequently records anatomical mapping and armour-location rulings, including the shared individual-creature anatomy. 

### Result

This adventure can exercise S-2/S-5, but it will require the actual anatomical mapping and tier policy to be instantiated in the adaptation.

**Readiness: 🟡 Adaptation/Integration**

---

# 11. Defence

The GURPS adventure explicitly uses Dodge and Parry, and specifically states that the Ice Troll may All-Out Attack with two claws **but no defence**. 

Tiwas S-6 is now ruled as:

* Active Defense;
* defender rolls;
* voluntary;
* uncapped;
* post-hoc mitigation;
* separate Defense roll per Effect;
* full Core Test consequences.



This is a major compatibility result.

### Important distinction

GURPS's **Dodge/Parry statistics do not transfer**.

But the adventure's underlying requirement—

> “the target gets an opportunity to mitigate an incoming combat consequence”

—is now represented by Tiwas S-6.

### Result

**Readiness: 🟢 Playtestable Now at subsystem level**

**Adaptation content still required:** define the relevant Tiwas defensive Skill(s)/Effects for the adventure.

---

# 12. Falling and Environmental Hazards

The adventure contains numerous physical hazards:

* cliffs;
* icy stairs;
* falling;
* cold;
* exhaustion;
* frozen passages;
* dangerous terrain.

For example, failure on the icy cliff causes 2d-2 damage, and failure on icy stairs causes 1d-2 damage. 

Tiwas has an important S-2 ruling for physical risks: a failed governing Core Test can provide the Location Index, while systemic threats can apply direct HP/Conditions without location. 

### Result

The **resolution architecture exists**.

The complete environmental-hazard grammar remains an integration/content dependency.

**Readiness: 🟡 Design-stage integration**

---

# 13. Fatigue and Resource Depletion

The adventure repeatedly uses GURPS FP:

* subtract 1 FP during the trek;
* subtract 2 FP breaking through ice;
* FP reaching zero causes collapse/death.



Tiwas has a fundamentally different resource model:

* Physical Energy;
* Mental Points;
* natural-roll resource cost;
* Overflow → HP;
* Recovery after every test.

This is not a simple one-for-one FP conversion.

### Important finding

The adventure's fatigue system is **not actually required as a separate Tiwas subsystem** if its fictional purpose can be represented by the existing PE/HP economy.

However, the exact adventure-specific conversion is not currently established.

**Readiness: 🟡 Adaptation Mapping Required**

This is therefore **not automatically evidence that a new fatigue subsystem must be designed.**

---

# 14. Healing

The adventure uses:

> First Aid or Physician

to restore HP after combat. Failure still produces 1 HP of recovery. 

Tiwas S-11 now provides a ruled healing architecture:

* explicit Skill Test;
* ordinary Core Test;
* wound magnitude modifies effective Skill;
* healing is an Extended Test;
* Margin accumulation;
* neutral failures;
* GM-set completion target.



### Result

The adventure's **healing requirement is now directly testable against S-11**.

The GURPS “restore 1d-3 HP / minimum 1” procedure itself should **not** be imported.

**Readiness: 🟢 Playtestable Now at subsystem level; adaptation required for the adventure-specific healing task.**

---

# 15. Incapacitation and Death

The adventure repeatedly distinguishes:

* still conscious;
* unconscious;
* death;
* permanent adventure termination.

Tiwas S-7 now has a ruled architecture:

* HP = 0 → forced incapacitation;
* no immediate death;
* incapacitation is HP-driven;
* revival uses skill tests;
* permanent loss occurs after failed revival attempts or voluntary permanent loss.



### Result

**Readiness: 🟢 Playtestable Now at subsystem level.**

This is another significant readiness improvement over the older Canonical v2.1 status.

---

# 16. Fear / Fright

The Blood Man requires a Fright Check, and the corpse scene requires a Fright Check at -2. 

The current Tiwas material does **not provide a fully enumerated fear/fright subsystem or established Condition implementation** sufficient to say that this is ready.

The fact that Tiwas has Mind attributes, MP, Skills and Effects does not itself constitute a Fright system.

### Result

**Readiness: 🔴 Missing / Design-stage dependency**

This is an important finding because the adventure is explicitly horror-inflected despite being mechanically simple.

---

# 17. Grappling

The Blood Man specifically relies upon:

1. wounding its target;
2. grappling;
3. applying Blood Seep;
4. applying ongoing corrosive damage.



This requires more than generic combat.

It needs a mechanical state representing:

> “Target is grappled.”

The current Tiwas material does not provide a complete grapple subsystem.

### Result

**Readiness: 🔴 Missing / Design-stage dependency**

This is one of the strongest concrete combat blockers exposed by the benchmark.

---

# 18. Time and Ongoing Effects

The adventure contains effects measured in:

* seconds;
* minutes;
* hours;
* days;
* spell durations;
* regeneration intervals.

Blood Seep, for example, operates per second, while Ice Troll regeneration operates per minute. 

The current Tiwas architecture identifies Time/Action Economy as a cross-cutting subsystem.

### Result

Because the adventure contains ongoing effects, **time is not optional if the full adventure is to be run faithfully as a Tiwas test**.

**Readiness: 🔴 Design-stage dependency**

---

# 19. Equipment and Encumbrance

The adventure depends heavily on equipment:

* swords;
* daggers;
* mace;
* axes;
* shield;
* crossbow;
* rope;
* grapple;
* torches;
* pitons;
* backpacks;
* clothing;
* armour;
* treasure.

The adventure also uses encumbrance mechanically, including climbing penalties per encumbrance level. 

The Tiwas Alpha corpus identifies Equipment and Tags as cross-cutting architecture, but the complete equipment system is not represented as a finished universal subsystem.

### Result

**Readiness: 🔴 Missing/Design-stage subsystem**

This is a major practical blocker because equipment is not incidental in this adventure—it is repeatedly used to determine what actions are possible.

---

# 20. Magic

The advanced pregenerated character is a spellcaster, and the character sheet contains spells such as:

* Fireball;
* Flame Jet;
* Minor Healing;
* Dark Vision;
* Light;
* Sense Danger;
* Warmth;
* Recover Energy.

The sheet also contains spell costs, durations and casting requirements. 

Tiwas's architectural direction is that magic should emerge through Advanced Skills rather than become a competing core engine.

But the actual **Magic/Special Ability grammar is not complete**.

### Result

**Readiness: 🔴 Missing / Design-stage subsystem**

The adventure can therefore serve as a strong future magic benchmark, but it cannot currently be run with the supplied spellcaster unchanged.

---

# 21. NPC and Creature Construction

The adventure contains explicit creature stat blocks.

The Ice Troll includes:

* ST;
* HP;
* Speed;
* DX;
* Will;
* IQ;
* Perception;
* HT;
* FP;
* DR;
* Dodge;
* Parry;
* attacks;
* traits;
* regeneration;
* skills.



The Blood Man has a similar block plus special Blood Seep behaviour. 

Tiwas S-12 has now established the architecture that automated systems use full 24-attribute generation, while tabletop/GM use an abbreviated representation, but actual creature templates remain content-authoring work. 

### Result

**Subsystem architecture: 🟢/🟡**

**Adventure-ready creature implementation: 🔴**

The benchmark therefore identifies **NPC content authoring**, rather than merely NPC architecture, as a real remaining workload.

---

# 22. Rewards and Progression

The adventure contains:

* treasure values;
* monetary reward;
* completion rewards;
* monster-defeat reward;
* loot-based reward;
* future-adventure currency.

The final treasure table lists values for the recovered objects, while completion awards additional characters. 

Tiwas already has General XP and quest/adventure rewards as a mechanism. 

### Result

**XP progression: 🟢 Playtestable Now**

**Currency/economy: 🔴 Missing/setting-content dependency**

The adventure's reward structure can therefore be used as a test of **General XP**, while the monetary economy should not be mistaken for an already-developed Tiwas economy.

---

# 23. Character Generation

The adventure provides pregenerated GURPS characters.

Their sheets contain:

* attributes;
* skills;
* advantages;
* disadvantages;
* racial traits;
* equipment;
* spells;
* wealth;
* languages;
* other GURPS-specific construction elements.

For example, King Coppertong has a large set of GURPS advantages/disadvantages, equipment and skills. 

Tiwas has the mathematical Core for:

* 24 attributes;
* Skill Caps;
* starting Skills;
* derived statistics;
* Advanced Skills.

But a complete **adventure-ready character-generation procedure and starting package system** is not equivalent to those mathematical rules.

### Result

**Readiness: 🟡 Core mathematics ready; character-generation implementation/content required.**

# 25. What the Adventure Actually Proves About Tiwas

## 25.1 The Core is not the problem

This benchmark strongly validates the value of the Tiwas Core architecture.

A large proportion of the adventure's apparently disparate GURPS tests reduce cleanly to:

> **ordinary Tiwas Core Tests.**

That includes climbing, searching, tracking, lockpicking, forced entry, survival, first aid, stealth, tactics, Will and DX-type tests.

This supports the architectural decision not to reproduce GURPS's numerous special-purpose resolution procedures.

---

## 25.2 S-1 is immediately useful

The adventure contains a genuine opposed contest:

> Stealth vs Perception.

That maps directly into S-1 without requiring a new contest engine.

This makes *Beyond the Vale of Madness* a practical S-1 playtest case rather than merely a theoretical validation case.

---

## 25.3 S-6 is now demonstrably relevant

The adventure's combat encounters require defensive response.

The new Active Defense ruling therefore directly services a real published adventure requirement. The defender's ability to decline defence is also compatible with the adventure's explicit All-Out Attack/no-defense concept at the architectural level, although the GURPS procedure itself should not be copied. 

---

# 26. The Most Important Gaps Exposed

## Priority 1 — Combat Integration

This is the dominant blocker.

The adventure cannot be fully played without:

* attack procedure;
* combat sequencing;
* movement/action timing;
* attack Skill/content;
* Effect application in combat;
* damage;
* grappling;
* ongoing effects.

---

## Priority 2 — Time / Action Economy

The adventure explicitly contains:

* tactical combat;
* seconds-long effects;
* minutes-long regeneration;
* spell durations;
* movement;
* prolonged activity.

Therefore Time is not merely a future convenience.

**This adventure demonstrates that Time is an actual playtest dependency.**

---

## Priority 3 — Equipment

The adventure assumes equipment is mechanically meaningful.

The player must know:

* what equipment exists;
* what it weighs;
* what it permits;
* what armour protects;
* what weapons do;
* what equipment can be used for climbing;
* how carrying capacity works.

The adventure therefore provides a concrete justification for completing the Equipment interface.

---

## Priority 4 — Grappling / Conditions

The Blood Man is particularly diagnostic.

Its intended combat loop is:

**Attack → Wound → Grapple → ongoing Blood Seep → possible death.**

That cannot be represented adequately with only generic HP damage.

This is precisely the kind of compound interaction that exposes whether Tiwas's universal subsystem architecture is actually complete.

---

## Priority 5 — Magic / Special Abilities

Enfys makes this unavoidable.

The adventure contains a complete spellcasting character rather than merely a magical treasure.

Therefore Tiwas needs a usable setting-level Special Ability/Magic interface before that character can be used without substantial substitution.

---

## Priority 6 — Fear / Mental Conditions

The adventure has explicit Fright Checks.

That makes fear a concrete test case for:

* Mind-domain resolution;
* Conditions;
* mental consequences.

It should not be allowed to remain hidden as an undefined “future condition system” if this adventure becomes a Tiwas benchmark.

---

---

# 28. Readiness Verdict

## 28.1 Can *Beyond the Vale of Madness* be playtested in Tiwas now?

### **Not as a fully self-contained, mechanically complete Tiwas conversion.**

But:

### **Yes, as a staged Tiwas readiness playtest.**

This distinction is important.

The adventure already provides enough ordinary tests and opposed tests to exercise the Core and S-1.

The newly ruled S-4 through S-11 material also means substantial portions of the adventure can now serve as **alpha subsystem tests**.

What is not yet available is the complete integrated layer required to run the adventure from paragraph 1 through paragraph 60 without making significant mechanical substitutions or GM inventions.

---

# 29. The Benchmark's Most Valuable Finding

The experiment has produced a better development metric than a simple checklist of “Tiwas systems remaining.”

The useful metric is:

> **Can a real published adventure encounter be resolved without the GM inventing a mechanic?**

Applied here:

| Benchmark layer       | Result                            |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Core resolution       | **Pass**                          |
| Ordinary tests        | **Pass**                          |
| Opposed tests         | **Pass**                          |
| Difficulty            | **Near-pass / interface work**    |
| Harm                  | **Partial**                       |
| Defence               | **Pass at alpha-rule level**      |
| Armour                | **Partial / content integration** |
| Healing               | **Pass at alpha-rule level**      |
| Incapacitation/death  | **Pass at alpha-rule level**      |
| Combat                | **Fail — incomplete integration** |
| Grappling             | **Fail**                          |
| Time/action economy   | **Fail**                          |
| Equipment/encumbrance | **Fail**                          |
| Magic                 | **Fail**                          |
| Fear/conditions       | **Fail**                          |
| NPC content           | **Partial / authoring required**  |
| Full adventure        | **Fail**                          |

---

# 30. Conclusions

## 30.1 Primary conclusion

**Beyond the Vale of Madness is a valid and useful Tiwas readiness benchmark.**

It is small enough to analyse completely, but mechanically broad enough to expose weaknesses that a simple Core-test exercise would miss.

## 30.2 What is already demonstrated

Tiwas has now demonstrated usable foundations for:

* universal d100 resolution;
* resource-costed testing;
* failure-driven progression;
* ordinary task tests;
* opposed contests;
* difficulty-side modification;
* location generation;
* Effects architecture;
* wounds/injury architecture;
* armour architecture;
* Active Defense;
* incapacitation/death;
* Extended Tests;
* healing.

The Alpha corpus explicitly records the current S-1 through S-11 table-play material and distinguishes it from Canonical status. 

## 30.3 What the benchmark says must still be developed

The highest-value remaining development targets exposed by this adventure are:

1. **Combat integration**
2. **Time / Action Economy**
3. **Equipment / Encumbrance**
4. **Grappling**
5. **Conditions**
6. **Fear / Fright**
7. **Magic / Special Abilities**
8. **NPC/creature content**
9. **Complete combat damage integration**
10. **Adventure-ready character-generation/content packages**

These are not arbitrary roadmap items. **This specific published adventure demonstrates why each is required.**

---

# 31. Final Readiness Statement

> **Tiwas has passed the “generic resolution engine” portion of the adventure benchmark, but has not yet passed the “complete RPG system” benchmark.**

The most significant result is that the benchmark has moved the project from:

> “Which RPG systems haven't we designed yet?”

toward the more useful question:

> **“Which real play situations still force a Tiwas GM to invent a rule?”**

For *Beyond the Vale of Madness*, the answer is now relatively precise:

**Combat, time/action sequencing, grappling/conditions, equipment/encumbrance, fear, magic, and complete NPC/creature implementation are the major remaining blockers.**

That makes this adventure suitable not merely as a future converted adventure, but as a **repeatable Tiwas development acceptance test**: when the remaining blockers have been resolved, the same adventure can be rerun and the benchmark can determine whether Tiwas has actually become capable of running a complete published scenario rather than merely possessing a large collection of individually designed subsystems.

---

# 32. Source and Authority Notes

### Primary sources

* *Beyond the Vale of Madness — GURPS*, J.C. Connors, v1.2. The adventure explicitly contains the numbered solo-adventure procedures, creature statistics, pregenerated characters, equipment, spells and reward structures. 
* `Tiwas-Alpha-Playtest-Corpus-2026-09-01.md`, which states that it is a one-off compilation of the currently Locked and Ruled material for alpha table use and does not itself alter authority. 

### Authority caution

The Alpha corpus contains **Non-canonical designer rulings** as well as Canonical/Locked rules. Those rulings are therefore treated in this report as **alpha-playtestable design**, not as promoted Canonical Tiwas rules. The corpus explicitly preserves that distinction. 

This distinction is important: **“playtestable now” does not mean “Canonical.”**

### Assumptions

1. All GURPS skill/attribute tests are replaced by the Tiwas Core Test, per your explicit instruction.
2. GURPS-specific statistics such as ST, DX, IQ, FP, Dodge, Parry, DR and GURPS damage dice are **requirements to be functionally replaced**, not Tiwas mechanics to be imported.
3. Adventure narrative, paragraph branching, named objects and setting material are not counted as Tiwas subsystem gaps unless they require a mechanical interface.
4. No attempt has been made to invent missing Tiwas mechanics merely to make the adventure playable.
5. The 1 September Alpha corpus is treated as the latest supplied working snapshot for the current design state, while preserving its Canonical/non-canonical distinction.

# Tiwas Adventure Readiness Audit

## *Beyond the Vale of Madness* as a Practical Systems Benchmark

**Audit date:** 2 September 2026
**Primary adventure source:** *Beyond the Vale of Madness — GURPS*, v1.2
**Primary Tiwas source:** *Tiwas — Alpha-Playtest Corpus*, 1 September 2026
**Assessment basis:** supplied sources only

---

# 1. Executive Summary

## 1.1 Overall finding

**Tiwas is not yet capable of running *Beyond the Vale of Madness* as a mechanically complete adventure.**

However, the adventure is a **very useful readiness benchmark**, because a substantial portion of its non-combat resolution can already be expressed through the Tiwas Core Test.

The adventure repeatedly uses ordinary skill/attribute tests for:

* climbing;
* survival;
* searching;
* tracking;
* stealth;
* lockpicking;
* forced entry;
* perception;
* first aid/physician;
* merchant appraisal;
* physical coordination;
* willpower/fear;
* opposed stealth;
* combat;
* damage;
* healing;
* fatigue/exhaustion;
* armour;
* incapacitation/death;
* magic;
* equipment;
* NPC/creature statistics;
* tactical positioning.

Under the audit rule that all GURPS skill and attribute tests become **ordinary Tiwas Core Tests**, the Core itself is already capable of carrying a large portion of the adventure's resolution load.

The principal blockers are therefore **not the basic resolution engine**.

They are the unresolved or insufficiently complete Universal Play systems surrounding it.

### 1.2 Readiness result

| Area                             | Current assessment                                                                   |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Basic d100 resolution            | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| Ordinary skill/attribute tests   | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| Failure XP / advancement         | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| Resource expenditure             | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| S-1 opposed resolution           | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| Difficulty modifiers             | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| Third-party adjudication         | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| Extended Tests                   | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| S-2 Zero-Step provider           | **Playtestable Now**, where invoked                                                  |
| Non-attack location provenance   | **Playtestable Now**, subject to existing ruling                                     |
| Basic HP injury                  | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| S-4 localized wounds             | **Design-Stage Dependency** for this adventure                                       |
| S-5 armour                       | **Design-Stage Dependency / mapping dependent**                                      |
| S-6 Defense                      | **Design-Stage Dependency for practical combat use**                                 |
| S-7 incapacitation/death         | **Playtestable Now at rule level; NPC/content implementation remains incomplete**    |
| S-8 difficulty                   | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| S-9/S-10 Extended Tests          | **Playtestable Now**                                                                 |
| S-11 healing                     | **Playtestable Now at subsystem level; adventure-specific healing mapping required** |
| Equipment                        | **Missing Subsystem**                                                                |
| Encumbrance                      | **Missing Subsystem**                                                                |
| Conditions                       | **Missing/Design-Stage dependency**                                                  |
| Combat attack/effect mapping     | **Design-Stage / Missing content**                                                   |
| NPC/creature construction        | **Design-Stage Dependency**                                                          |
| Magic                            | **Missing Subsystem**                                                                |
| Tactical movement/action economy | **Missing Subsystem**                                                                |
| GURPS-specific damage model      | **Must be replaced by Tiwas mapping**                                                |
| Adventure branching/content      | **Adventure Content Only**                                                           |

The most important conclusion is:

> **The adventure does not demonstrate that Tiwas needs a better Core Test. It demonstrates that Tiwas needs its surrounding consequence, combat, equipment, condition, magic, and NPC/content layers completed.**

---

# 2. Audit Objective and Method

## 2.1 Objective

The adventure is treated as an **external functional benchmark**.

The question is not:

> "How do we convert GURPS into Tiwas?"

The question is:

> "What does this adventure require a game system to accomplish, and can current Tiwas accomplish that function?"

This distinction is critical.

The adventure uses GURPS terminology such as DX, ST, FP, Dodge, Parry, DR, damage dice, Fright Checks and spell levels. These are **not imported into Tiwas**.

They are treated as evidence of required functionality.

For example:

> GURPS "make a Climbing roll"

becomes:

> **Tiwas must be able to resolve a climbing task through the ordinary Core Test.**

The GURPS procedure itself has no normative authority over Tiwas.

---

## 2.2 Tiwas authority hierarchy

The Alpha-Playtest Corpus explicitly states that it is a dated table-ready assembly rather than a new source of authority. Canonical/Locked material remains authoritative, while the Part B subsystem material consists of recorded **non-canonical designer rulings**. 

This audit therefore distinguishes:

1. **Canonical / Locked**
2. **Ruled non-canonical**
3. **Open / not table-ready**
4. **Adventure-specific adaptation**
5. **Pure adventure content**

The existence of a subsystem name does **not** automatically establish readiness.

---
