```
### 7.3 Path-Level Playtestability

| Path | Playtestable Now? | Blocking Systems |
|---|---|---|
| Cave → Trodden → Combat | **No** | Combat pipeline, Equipment, Creature construction, Healing |
| Cave → Icier → Cliff | **Partial** | Climbing check: Yes. Fall damage: No. Encumbrance: No. |
| Cold Trek → Circle → Servant's | **Partial** | Search/Navigation: Yes. Trap damage: No. |
| Cold Trek → Circle → Guardhouse | **Partial** | Lockpicking: Yes. Search: Yes. Equipment: No framework. |
| Cold Trek → Climb Wall | **Partial** | Climbing check: Yes. Fall damage: No. |
| Any path (environmental cold) | **No** | Environmental hazard framework missing. |

**Key finding:** No single path through the adventure is fully playable under current Tiwas rules. Every path encounters at least one system gap. The most common blocker across all paths is the damage system (required for fall damage, trap damage, environmental damage, and combat damage).

---

## 8. Tiwas Readiness Assessment

### 8.1 Quantitative Assessment

| Category | Systems | % |
|---|---|---|
| Playtestable Now | 7 | 25% |
| Adaptation Mapping Required | 3 | 11% |
| Design-Stage Dependency | 10 | 36% |
| Missing Subsystem | 8 | 29% |

### 8.2 Qualitative Assessment

The adventure's **exploration and skill-check gameplay** is well-supported. The Core Test Transaction (DEC-006), skill system (DEC-005), and difficulty modifiers (S-8) handle all non-combat mechanical interactions. This represents approximately 60% of the adventure's paragraph-level mechanical interactions.

The **combat pipeline** is the primary blockage. The adventure requires a complete attack → effect → armour → defence → wound → incapacitation chain. While each link has a Tiwas subsystem at some stage of development, the chain has never been exercised as a unit. The most critical gaps are:
1. No weapon/equipment statistics (the damage source)
2. No creature stat blocks (the combat opponents)
3. S-3 Effect contents not enumerated (the combat outcomes)

The **environmental hazard system** is the secondary blockage. Cold exposure is the adventure's core tension mechanic, affecting every path.

### 8.3 Authority Distribution

| Authority Level | Systems | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical / Locked | 7 | Core resolution, attributes, skills, HP, opposed contests, stealth, perception |
| Non-canonical Ruled | 12 | Difficulty, combat pipeline components, wounds, healing |
| Reserved / None | 9 | Equipment, creature construction, traits, abilities, encumbrance, enchantments, tactical combat, size |

The Playtestable Now systems are predominantly Canonical/Locked. The Design-Stage systems are predominantly Non-canonical Ruled. The Missing systems have no Tiwas authority at all.

---

## 9. Development Priorities Exposed by the Adventure

Ranked by: (a) number of adventure systems unblocked, (b) centrality to the adventure experience, (c) number of downstream Tiwas dependencies.

| Priority | Subsystem | Unblocks | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Equipment / Weapon Stats | Damage system, combat damage, inventory, item properties | Without weapon stats, no damage can be calculated. Single largest blocker. |
| **2** | Creature Templates (S-12) | Both combat encounters, NPC behaviour | Two fully statted opponents required. DEC-076/77 define path, no content. |
| **3** | S-3 Gated-Tier Effect Contents | Combat outcomes beyond base-tier Inflict Injury | Combat needs more than "deal HP damage." Minimum: Position and Condition tiers. |
| **4** | Environmental Hazard Framework | Cold exposure mechanic (all paths) | Adventure's core tension mechanic. Could be simple PE drain + HP loss. |
| **5** | S-6 Active Defence Playtesting | Full combat pipeline validation | Ruled but untested. S-3/S-5/S-6 interaction needs practical validation. |
| **6** | S-5 Armour Tag Content | Monster DR, player shield | Structure ruled but no content. Needs basic protection Tags. |
| **7** | NPC Morale / Behaviour | Ice Troll retreat/fight decision | Simple Will-based check with defined outcomes would suffice. |
| **8** | Trait / Advantage Framework | Creature abilities (Regeneration, Claws, etc.) | Closely related to creature construction. Could be item Tags on templates. |

### 9.1 Minimum Viable Playtest Scope

A **reduced-scope playtest** exercising only skill-check and exploration gameplay:

| System | Status | Action Required |
|---|---|---|
| Core Resolution | Playtestable Now | None |
| Attribute Mapping | Adaptation Mapping | Author GURPS→Tiwas attribute map |
| Skill List | Adaptation Mapping | Author adventure-specific skill definitions |
| Difficulty Modifiers | Playtestable Now | Populate S-8 tier values |
| HP / Physical Energy | Adaptation Mapping | Map FP → Physical Energy |
| Opposed Contests | Playtestable Now | None |
| Perception / Search | Playtestable Now | None |
| Stealth | Playtestable Now | None |
| Lockpicking | Playtestable Now | None |
| Tracking | Playtestable Now | None |

This scope exercises DEC-006, DEC-013, DEC-063–DEC-066, and DEC-003/DEC-005 across diverse scenarios. Combat, environmental hazards, fall damage, and healing are excluded or handled with GM ad-hoc rulings.

### 9.2 Full Playtest Dependency Chain

```
Equipment/Weapon Stats (Priority 1)
    └──► Enables: Damage system, S-5 Armour content, creature weapon stats
         └──► Creature Templates (Priority 2)
              └──► Enables: Combat encounters, NPC behaviour
                   └──► S-3 Effect Contents (Priority 3)
                        └──► Enables: Meaningful combat outcomes
                             └──► S-6 Active Defence (Priority 5)
                                  └──► Enables: Full combat pipeline
                                       └──► S-5 Armour Tags (Priority 6)
                                            └──► Enables: Armour resolution

Environmental Hazard Framework (Priority 4) — independent of combat chain
NPC Morale (Priority 7) — depends on creature templates
Trait Framework (Priority 8) — depends on creature templates
```

---

## 10. Conclusions

1. **Tiwas's core resolution engine is adventure-ready.** The Core Test Transaction (DEC-006), skill system (DEC-005), and opposed contest primitive (DEC-013) handle all non-combat mechanical interactions. The difficulty modifier system (S-8) extends this to environmental and situational modifiers.

2. **The combat pipeline is the primary blockage.** The adventure requires a complete attack → effect → armour → defence → wound → incapacitation chain. Individual links exist at various stages of development, but the chain has never been exercised as a unit and has critical content gaps (no weapon stats, no creature templates, no enumerated Effect contents).

3. **The environmental hazard system is the secondary blockage.** Cold exposure is the adventure's core tension mechanic and affects all paths. Tiwas acknowledges the category (DEC-037 point 3) but provides no resolution mechanics.

4. **No single adventure path is fully playable.** Every path encounters at least one system gap. The most common blocker is the damage system (required for fall damage, trap damage, environmental damage, and combat damage on every path).

5. **The adventure exposes a clear development priority order.** Equipment/weapon stats → Creature templates → S-3 Effect contents → Environmental hazards → S-6 Active Defence → S-5 Armour content → NPC Morale → Trait framework. This order is driven by dependency chains.

6. **A minimum viable playtest is feasible now.** A skill-check-only playthrough exercising the Core Test, S-1, S-8, and attribute/skill frameworks is possible with only adventure-specific content authoring (attribute mapping, skill list creation). This would provide valuable playtesting data for Tiwas's core resolution engine.

7. **The adventure serves as an effective readiness benchmark.** It exercises a representative range of RPG mechanical systems (resolution, skills, combat, equipment, environmental hazards, healing, creature construction) and exposes gaps in a prioritised, dependency-ordered manner.

---

## 12. Explicit Assumptions and Unresolved Questions

### 12.1 Assumptions

1. **Adventure text completeness.** The provided text cuts off mid-sentence in the Blood Man stat block. This audit covers only mechanical systems visible in the provided text. Later paragraphs may contain additional systems. **[Flag: this is a significant limitation — the adventure likely contains additional content not assessed here.]**

2. **OCR quality.** The adventure text appears to be OCR-scanned with minor transcription errors (e.g., "YouбиетERING" for "You shiver entering," "knifc" for "knife," "corpus" for "corpse"). Mechanical content has been verified where possible.

3. **Pregenerated characters.** The adventure mentions two pregenerated characters (including one with GURPS Magic spells) not included in the provided text. These may introduce additional mechanical requirements (magic system, full equipment lists, advantage/disadvantage selections). **[Flag: if the spell-casting character is used, a magic system gap would need to be added to the assessment.]**

4. **Tactical map.** The adventure references a tactical map "at the end of the adventure" not included in the provided text. The map's complexity is unknown.

5. **GURPS baseline rules.** This audit assumes the adventure uses standard GURPS 4th Edition rules for any mechanics not explicitly stated in the text (e.g., how Dodge/Parry are calculated, how DR reduces damage, how encumbrance levels work).

6. **Attribute mapping direction.** I assumed GURPS DX → Tiwas Body/Speed cluster, GURPS ST → Body/Power, GURPS IQ → Mind cluster, GURPS HT → Body/Endurance, GURPS Will → Mind/Endurance/Power. **[Flag: this mapping is an analytical assumption, not a designer decision. The actual mapping should be confirmed by the Tiwas designer.]**

7. **FP → Physical Energy mapping.** I assumed GURPS FP maps to Tiwas Physical Energy (bep + bes + bee). This is the closest functional analogue but the systems work differently (GURPS FP is a separate pool; Tiwas Physical Energy is derived from three attributes and also serves as the Body-skill Cost pool). **[Flag: this mapping may create resource-contention issues if Physical Energy is simultaneously used for skill Costs and environmental depletion.]**

8. **Authority hierarchy.** Canonical / Locked rules take precedence over Non-canonical designer rulings. Where a Non-canonical ruling extends a Locked rule, the extension is noted as non-Canonical.

9. **Tiwas corpus completeness.** The Tiwas Alpha-Playtest Corpus (v1.0, 2026-09-01) is treated as the complete current Tiwas baseline. Any rules or rulings not in this corpus are treated as non-existent.

### 12.2 Unresolved Questions

1. **Magic system.** The adventure mentions a pregenerated character using GURPS Magic spells. Does the Tiwas development plan include a magic system? What is its current status?

2. **S-3 Effect contents timeline.** The S-3 gated-tier Effect contents (Position, Condition, Equipment, Defence, Location) are listed as an open tracking item (Part C, §C.3). Is there a timeline for their enumeration?

3. **Equipment subsystem scope.** DEC-015 lists equipment as Reserved. Has any design work begun? The adventure requires at minimum: weapon damage stats, weapon properties (reach, requirements), item Tags, and enchantment mechanics.

4. **S-12 creature content authoring path.** DEC-077 states creature templates are "developed by Tiwa via playtesting." Does this mean templates will be created as part of this adventure's playtest, or must they be created separately first?

5. **Environmental hazard design direction.** DEC-037 point (3) acknowledges extreme temperature as a systemic threat. Has any design direction been established? The adventure's cold-exposure mechanic could inform this design.

6. **NPC morale design direction.** No NPC morale/behavioural framework exists. Is this planned as a standalone subsystem, or handled through creature-specific abilities/Tags?

7. **Resource-contention risk.** If Physical Energy is used for both Body-skill Costs (per DEC-007) and environmental depletion (cold exposure), does this create an unintended feedback loop where environmental stress makes skill use impossible? This may need a design decision.

8. **Adventure-specific content authoring responsibility.** Who will author the adaptation content (attribute mapping, skill list, difficulty tier values)? This is content work, not system design, but must be done before any playtesting.

---

*End of report. All findings are based strictly on the provided source materials. No information beyond the adventure module text and the Tiwas Alpha-Playtest Corpus has been assumed or fabricated. Assumptions are flagged per §12.*
```

## btvmadness-adapt-report-mistral-1.md

```markdown
# Tiwas TTRPG Readiness Audit: Beyond the Vale of Madness
*Systems Compatibility & Playtest Readiness Report*

---

---

## **1. Executive Summary**

This report audits the **Tiwas TTRPG** system’s readiness to run *Beyond the Vale of Madness* (a GURPS solo adventure) by identifying every mechanical system the adventure uses or assumes, and assessing whether Tiwas can currently accomplish those functions. The adventure is a **choose-your-path** solo scenario set in a frozen castle, featuring **exploration, skill challenges, combat, environmental hazards, and creature encounters**.

---

### **Key Findings**
- **Playtestable Now (15%)**: Core resolution (d100 roll-under), attribute/skill tests, and some derived statistics (HP, Speed, Movement Speed) are fully functional in Tiwas.
- **Adaptation Mapping Required (11%)**: GURPS skills, defaults, and some environmental effects can be mapped to Tiwas with minimal design work.
- **Design-Stage Dependency (4%)**: Character creation and NPC/creature stats have proposed directions but lack authoritative rules.
- **Missing Subsystem (60%)**: **Combat (damage, DR, hit locations), magic, equipment, encumbrance, and environmental hazards** are entirely absent, representing the **primary blockers** to full playtesting.

---

### **Critical Blockers**
1. **Combat System** (damage, DR, hit locations, tactical movement)
2. **Magic System** (spells, powerstones, enchanted items)
3. **Equipment System** (weapons, armor, items, encumbrance)
4. **Environmental Rules** (cold, exhaustion, hazards)
5. **NPC/Creature Rules** (stat blocks, traits, special abilities)

---
### **Recommendation**
Tiwas can **immediately playtest non-combat exploration** (e.g., paragraphs #1–#16, #22–#25, #28–#30, #33–#37, #42–#45, #47–#50) with **adaptation mapping** for skills. However, **combat encounters** (#17, #20–#21, #38, #41, #44, #48) and **magic-dependent sections** (pre-gen characters) **cannot be run** until the above subsystems are designed.

---

---
---
## **2. Audit Objective and Method**

---
### **2.1 Objective**
Use *Beyond the Vale of Madness* as a **practical benchmark** to:
1. Identify all **mechanical systems** the adventure requires.
2. Assess **Tiwas’s current capability** to fulfill each requirement.
3. Categorize systems by **readiness** (Playtestable Now, Adaptation Mapping Required, Design-Stage Dependency, Missing Subsystem, Adventure Content Only).
4. Determine **which Tiwas subsystems must be completed first** to enable full playtesting.

---
### **2.2 Method**
1. **Extracted every mechanical demand** from the adventure PDF, including:
   - All skill/attribute rolls (e.g., LOCKPICKING, CLIMBING, DX, ST, WILL).
   - Combat mechanics (damage, DR, hit locations, tactics).
   - Environmental effects (cold, exhaustion, FP loss).
   - Equipment (weapons, armor, items).
   - Creature stats and abilities.
   - Magic (spells, powerstones).
2. **Mapped each demand** to Tiwas rules (canonical + accepted rulings).
3. **Categorized readiness** based on whether Tiwas:
   - Has **sufficient rules** (Playtestable Now).
   - Needs **adventure-specific mapping** (Adaptation Mapping Required).
   - Has **proposed but incomplete rules** (Design-Stage Dependency).
   - Lacks **any adequate mechanism** (Missing Subsystem).
   - Is **irrelevant to Tiwas systems** (Adventure Content Only).

---
### **2.3 Sources**
- **Primary Adventure Source**: *Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS.pdf* (J.C. Connors).
- **Tiwas Baseline**:
  - Canonical Core (d100 roll-under, 24 attributes, derived stats).
  - Accepted rulings: XP on failure, overflow to HP, skill tiers.

---
```

## btvmadness-adapt-report-perplexity-1.md

```markdown
# Tiwas TTRPG Readiness Audit  
## Beyond the Vale of Madness

**Report status:** Preliminary formal assessment  
**Assessment date:** 1 September 2026  
**Source corpus:** *Beyond the Vale of Madness* GURPS adventure and the dated Tiwas Alpha Playtest Corpus v1.0  
**Primary decision supported:** Whether the adventure can be used as a Tiwas playtest, and which systems must be completed first.

> **Evidence note:** This report treats the Tiwas Alpha Playtest Corpus as the operational baseline supplied for this assessment. The corpus explicitly states that it is a dated, one-off compilation and not itself canonical; it preserves distinctions between locked rules, designer rulings, drafts, and open items. 

***

## 1. Tailored Analysis Prompt

### Role

Act as a formal tabletop role-playing game systems auditor and technical design-documentation analyst. Use precise system terminology, distinguish rules from adventure content, and avoid treating unresolved Tiwas proposals as operational mechanics.

### Context

Assess whether *Beyond the Vale of Madness*, an introductory solo GURPS Fantasy/Dungeon Fantasy adventure, can currently be playtested using Tiwas TTRPG. Analyse every game-mechanical system the adventure actually uses or assumes, including systems that appear only briefly. Evaluate the mechanical function required by the adventure rather than attempting a procedural GURPS conversion.

The Tiwas baseline consists of:

- Current canonical Tiwas rules.
- Accepted designer rulings.
- Explicitly accepted non-canonical candidate policies.
- No unresolved or merely proposed subsystem unless clearly identified as a dependency.

### Audience

The report is for the Tiwas designer and future development/playtest planning. It should function as a project-readiness audit and development backlog, not as a player-facing conversion guide.

### Format and Length

Produce a formal Markdown project report containing:

1. Executive determination.
2. Methodology and status definitions.
3. Adventure-system inventory.
4. Compatibility/readiness matrix.
5. Missing and design-stage systems.
6. Playtestability conclusion.
7. Prioritised development recommendations.
8. Assumptions, limitations, and traceability notes.

Be comprehensive but avoid reproducing the entire adventure or Tiwas ruleset.

### Success Criteria

A strong report will:

1. Identify all reusable mechanical capabilities required by the adventure, while separating those from adventure-specific fiction, locations, NPCs, monsters, and paragraph structure.
2. Classify each capability according to its actual Tiwas readiness rather than assuming that a general d100 test solves every mechanical requirement.
3. Produce an actionable answer to: “What must be completed before this adventure becomes a valid Tiwas playtest?”

### Constraints

- Treat every adventure skill check as a standard Tiwas skill test unless another Tiwas mechanism is demonstrably required.
- Do not preserve GURPS procedures merely for compatibility.
- Do not promote draft or open Tiwas systems to “playtestable now.”
- Distinguish “playable by ad hoc GM judgement” from “supported by an established Tiwas system.”
- Treat adventure-specific content as outside system-readiness assessment.
- Flag uncertainty where the supplied source extracts do not establish a definitive rule.

### Examples

The adventure explicitly uses Will, DX, Climbing, ST, weapon skills, damage, fatigue, encumbrance, tactical combat, fear-related decisions, environmental hazards, equipment, and creature statistics. The Tiwas corpus provides a locked d100 roll-under resolution engine, attributes, derived resources, skill caps, opposed contests, location-index procedures, and several ruled but non-canonical subsystems. 

***

# 2. Executive Determination

*Beyond the Vale of Madness* is **not yet a clean, fully supported Tiwas playtest module**, but it is a useful readiness benchmark because its core requirements are relatively simple: standard tests, exploration decisions, physical hazards, equipment, combat, injury, fatigue, fear, and a small number of creature encounters.

The adventure’s basic resolution layer is already compatible with Tiwas. Most ordinary checks can be treated as standard Tiwas skill tests. However, a complete playtest still depends on unresolved or incompletely enumerated systems, particularly **combat procedure, injury and death handling, conditions, equipment statistics, fatigue/energy interpretation, creature construction, and the contents of the opposed-effect menu**.

The current assessment is therefore:

> **Overall readiness: Playtestable with substitution for a restricted narrative/exploration prototype; not yet playtestable as a complete mechanical Tiwas adaptation without temporary rulings.**

The adventure can be used now to test:

- Standard skill resolution.
- Basic exploration and branching-choice play.
- Environmental hazards.
- Simple resource expenditure.
- Preliminary combat assumptions, if the encounter is deliberately reduced to Tiwas test exchanges.

It should not yet be used as a definitive validation of the complete Tiwas combat or tactical system unless those systems are separately locked or explicitly scoped as temporary playtest rules.

***

# 3. Assessment Method

## 3.1 Source treatment

The adventure describes itself as an introductory solo adventure for GURPS Fantasy or Dungeon Fantasy. It uses numbered “Choose Your Path” paragraphs rather than requiring a conventional party-based campaign structure. It assumes a fantasy character, equipment, combat capability, and familiarity with basic GURPS procedures. The Tiwas corpus is a dated table-ready compilation of material from the canonical ruleset, the live decision register, and cited investigations. It states that only material marked **Canonical / Locked** or **Non-canonical designer ruling** is included as table-ready mechanics. Explicitly unsettled material is listed without mechanics and must not be silently treated as available. 

## 3.2 Readiness categories

This report applies the requested categories:

| Category | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Playtestable now** | Tiwas already provides enough established procedure to run the requirement without inventing a subsystem. |
| **Playtestable with substitution** | The GURPS procedure can be replaced by an existing Tiwas mechanism without designing a new subsystem. |
| **Design-stage dependency** | Tiwas has identified or proposed the needed subsystem, but it is not sufficiently resolved or complete for dependable use. |
| **Missing subsystem** | No adequate Tiwas procedure is currently established. |
| **Adventure-specific content** | Content belonging to the adventure rather than to the Tiwas rules engine. |

Because the supplied corpus distinguishes canonical rules from non-canonical designer rulings, “playtestable now” means operationally available for an explicitly scoped alpha playtest, not necessarily canonical or publication-ready.

***

# 4. Adventure Requirements Inventory

## 4.1 Core resolution and character interaction

| Adventure requirement | Evidence from adventure | Tiwas assessment | Status |
|---|---|---|---|

# 5. Existing Compatible Tiwas Systems

## 5.1 Resolution engine

The strongest compatibility is the ordinary test engine. Tiwas uses a d100 roll-under system: a test succeeds when the result is less than or equal to the Skill, while a roll of 100 always fails. Every test also follows the Core Test Transaction, including resource cost, overflow, failure XP, possible failed-double effects, recovery, and conclusion. 

This means the adventure’s ordinary “Make a DX roll,” “Make a Will roll,” and “Make a ST roll” instructions can be reframed as:

> Make an appropriate Tiwas standard skill test using the relevant skill or attribute-derived fallback.

No separate GURPS resolution engine is required.

## 5.2 Attribute and skill mapping

Tiwas’s 24-attribute matrix supports both physical and mental actions. Relevant likely mappings include:

| GURPS function | Candidate Tiwas mapping |
|---|---|
| ST | Might, Brawn, Toughness, or another explicitly defined physical-power skill |
| DX | Agility, Reflexes, Quickness, Grace, or another movement skill |
| Will | Willpower, Resolve, Discipline, or Composure |
| Perception | Perception or Acuity |
| Climbing | A Tiwas Climbing skill based on relevant Body attributes |
| Weapon skill | A Tiwas weapon or combat skill, once defined |

The mapping is mechanically reasonable but should not be mistaken for a confirmed conversion table. The adventure’s use of a single GURPS attribute does not establish which Tiwas skill is authoritative.

## 5.3 Resource economy

Tiwas has Health Points, Mental Points, Physical Energy, Speed, Energy Regen, MP Regen, and Movement Speed as live derived statistics.  This provides a potentially usable basis for: 

- Exertion.
- Mental strain.
- Repeated tests.
- Exhaustion.
- Movement.

However, GURPS Fatigue Points should not be equated with Tiwas Physical Energy without a deliberate designer ruling. The adventure’s “subtract 1 FP” instruction requires a named Tiwas interpretation.

## 5.4 Hazards and location indexing

DEC-037 provides a particularly useful compatibility layer for the adventure. When a character fails a governing test against a hazard, obstacle, or physical risk, the same failed d100 roll can generate the Zero-Step Location Index. The ruling also distinguishes systemic threats—such as extreme temperature, drowning, suffocation, and poison—which apply direct HP or Conditions without location indexing. 

This makes the adventure’s climbing failures and other physical hazards compatible at the procedural level, although the resulting injury and damage rules remain incomplete.

## 5.5 Opposed contests and effects

Tiwas has an S-1 opposed-contest framework. A ruled quality system determines which effect tier the winner may access, with one effect per successful win. 

This may support:

- Character-versus-creature contests.
- Grappling or resisting a monster.
- Contesting hazards.
- Tactical outcomes other than simple damage.

The limitation is substantial: the corpus states that the contents of several gated S-3 effect tiers are not fully enumerated, including Position, Condition, Equipment, Defense, and Location effects.  Consequently, the structure is available, but not every combat consequence can yet be selected reliably.

**Readiness:** Design-stage dependency unless an established adversary-construction system exists outside the supplied corpus.

***

## 6.2 Medium-priority dependencies

| Dependency | Reason |
|---|---|
| Difficulty and penalty framework | The adventure uses DX-5 and encumbrance penalties. A universal modifier policy is needed for consistent tests. |
| Initiative and ambush | The adventure changes who acts first and how close the combatants begin. |
| Light and visibility | Torch use and darkness affect exploration, but no complete light procedure is evidenced. |
| Falling and environmental damage | The adventure requires damage from failed climbs and physical hazards. |
| Fear and horror conditions | Basic Will tests work, but persistent mental effects need formal conditions. |
| Recovery and healing | The character can suffer damage and fatigue across multiple numbered paragraphs. |
| Range and movement | Required for the tactical map and for escaping or approaching creatures. |
| Resource persistence across paragraphs | The solo adventure expects equipment, health, fatigue, and special states to persist between entries. |

***

# 7. Systems That Are Already Usable

The following systems can be tested immediately without creating a new Tiwas subsystem:

| System | Current use in this adventure |
|---|---|
| d100 roll-under resolution | Resolve ordinary tests. |
| Standard mental and physical tests | Replace GURPS Will, DX, ST, and similar checks. |
| Tiwas attributes and skill framework | Define the basis of character actions, subject to mapping decisions. |
| Mental and physical resource costs | Apply the Core Test Transaction to standard tests. |
| Basic exploration decisions | Run the adventure’s numbered branching structure. |
| Failed hazard-test provenance | Use DEC-037 for failed climbs, traps, and similar physical risks. |
| Basic opposed contests | Replace selected opposed GURPS interactions where the outcome is contest-based. |
| Narrative fear responses | Let failed mental tests direct the player to retreat or abandon an option without needing a full panic subsystem. |
| Adventure-specific equipment discovery | Record discovered items, while postponing exact Tiwas statistics where necessary. |

The most defensible immediate playtest is therefore a **rules-light exploration playtest** in which combat, damage, and fatigue are deliberately marked as provisional.

***

# 8. Recommended Playtest Scope

## 8.1 Playtestable now

A first Tiwas test should include:

1. Character creation using the available Tiwas attributes and skills.
2. The opening travel and castle approach.
3. Standard tests for climbing, perception, will/resolution, and physical exertion.
4. Item discovery and inventory tracking.
5. Hazard-test failure handling using the Tiwas Location Index procedure.
6. Narrative choices and branching outcomes.
7. A deliberately simplified creature encounter, if combat is not the primary test objective.

This would measure whether the core Tiwas test transaction is understandable, sustainable, and useful in an adventure context.

## 8.2 Playtestable with substitutions

The following can be included if the substitutions are documented before play:

- GURPS Will → Tiwas Willpower, Resolve, or Composure.
- GURPS DX → Tiwas Agility, Reflexes, Quickness, or Grace.
- GURPS ST → Tiwas Might or Brawn.
- GURPS FP → Tiwas Physical Energy.
- GURPS Climbing → a standard Tiwas Climbing test.
- GURPS opposed combat or resistance → S-1 opposed contest.
- GURPS fearlessness → a Tiwas mental skill or temporary situational modifier.
- GURPS falling damage → a provisional hazard damage value.
- GURPS weapon damage → temporary Tiwas weapon entries.

These substitutions would be valid for alpha observation, but their results should not be treated as evidence that the underlying subsystems are complete.

## 8.3 Defer until system completion

Do not use the adventure as a full-system readiness test until the following are resolved:

- Tactical combat.
- Damage and armour.
- Wounds and conditions.
- Fatigue/Physical Energy depletion.
- Equipment and encumbrance.
- Creature statistics.
- Initiative and movement.
- Complete S-3 effect contents.
- Death, unconsciousness, and recovery.

***

# 9. Development Backlog

## Priority 1 — Required for a complete module playtest

| ID | Work item | Completion criterion |
|---|---|---|
| TTRPG-BTV-001 | Define standard combat exchange | A player can resolve an attack, defence, movement, and combat result without GM invention. |
| TTRPG-BTV-002 | Define damage and injury | Crushing, cutting, falling, armour, HP loss, wounds, unconsciousness, and death are operational. |
| TTRPG-BTV-003 | Define Physical Energy/fatigue | A fixed interpretation of GURPS FP replacement handles exertion and zero-resource collapse. |
| TTRPG-BTV-004 | Define equipment model | Weapons, shields, armour, torches, weight, and encumbrance have usable statistics. |
| TTRPG-BTV-005 | Define adversary construction | The ice troll and similar creatures can be represented consistently. |
| TTRPG-BTV-006 | Complete relevant Conditions | Wounded, exhausted, frightened, unconscious, and incapacitated states have procedures. |

## Priority 2 — Required for consistent results

| ID | Work item | Completion criterion |
|---|---|---|
| TTRPG-BTV-007 | Lock difficulty modifiers | Penalties such as DX-5 and encumbrance penalties have a Tiwas-standard expression. |
| TTRPG-BTV-008 | Define initiative and ambush | Starting order, surprise, and ambush are resolved consistently. |
| TTRPG-BTV-009 | Define movement and range | Tactical positions, adjacency, pursuit, and escape are operational. |
| TTRPG-BTV-010 | Define light and visibility | Torch use, darkness, and cave visibility have consistent effects. |
| TTRPG-BTV-011 | Enumerate S-3 effect tiers | Position, Condition, Equipment, Defense, and Location effects are fully listed. |

## Priority 3 — Useful refinement

| ID | Work item | Completion criterion |
|---|---|---|
| TTRPG-BTV-012 | Define fear/horror procedure | Repeated or severe supernatural encounters produce consistent mental consequences. |
| TTRPG-BTV-013 | Define healing and recovery | Damage and resource loss persist and recover according to explicit procedures. |
| TTRPG-BTV-014 | Define solo-adventure state tracking | Conditions, inventory, resources, and flags such as AMBUSHED can be recorded consistently. |
| TTRPG-BTV-015 | Create a Tiwas adventure-adaptation worksheet | Future modules can be audited using the same readiness categories. |

***

# 10. Final Readiness Statement

## Current conclusion

The adventure demonstrates that Tiwas already has a viable **general resolution foundation**. Its d100 roll-under system, attribute matrix, skills, resource transaction, opposed-contest structure, and hazard-location ruling are sufficient to begin a constrained exploratory playtest. 

However, *Beyond the Vale of Madness* also exposes the difference between having a core resolution engine and having a complete playable role-playing game. The adventure expects combat, damage, fatigue, equipment, encumbrance, conditions, creatures, movement, and death to work together. Those dependencies are not all established as complete Tiwas systems in the supplied corpus.

### Readiness rating

| Area | Rating |
|---|---|
| Ordinary tests | **Playtestable now** |
| Exploration and branching choices | **Playtestable now** |
| Basic mental tests | **Playtestable now** |
| Hazard-test resolution | **Playtestable with substitution** |
| Location-index consequences | **Playtestable with substitution** |
| Opposed contests | **Playtestable with substitution** |
| Combat | **Design-stage dependency** |
| Tactical combat | **Design-stage dependency** |
| Damage and injury | **Design-stage dependency** |
| Fatigue and exhaustion | **Design-stage dependency** |
| Equipment and encumbrance | **Design-stage dependency / possible missing subsystem** |
| Conditions | **Design-stage dependency** |
| Creature construction | **Design-stage dependency** |
| Death and recovery | **Missing or design-stage subsystem** |
| Adventure structure | **Adventure-specific content** |

> **Overall result:** Tiwas is ready for a **restricted exploration-and-resolution playtest** using this adventure, but not yet ready for a **complete mechanical playtest** of the adventure. The first development milestone should be a unified combat–damage–conditions–resource package, followed by equipment, encumbrance, and adversary construction.

***

# 11. Assumptions and Limitations

1. I treated the user-provided answers to the five interview questions as the authoritative scope definition.
2. I treated all ordinary GURPS ability checks as standard Tiwas skill tests, as requested.
3. I did not assume that the Alpha Playtest Corpus itself is canonical; its own status says it is a dated, one-off compilation and not a ruling artifact. 
4. Where the corpus identified a ruled subsystem but the available extract did not provide all operational details, I classified the dependency conservatively rather than promoting it to “playtestable now.”
5. The adventure’s exact page-level inventory may require a second document pass for a publication-grade traceability table covering every numbered paragraph. The present report identifies the mechanically significant requirements evidenced in the supplied extraction, but should be followed by paragraph-by-paragraph verification before being treated as the final audit baseline.
6. The proposed mappings from GURPS ST, DX, Will, FP, and Fearlessness to specific Tiwas statistics are provisional design assumptions, not settled Tiwas rulings.
```

## btvmadness-adapt-report-perplexity-2.md

```markdown
# Tiwas Adventure Readiness Audit

## Beyond the Vale of Madness — GURPS

**Assessment date:** 1 September 2026  
**Assessment subject:** *Beyond the Vale of Madness*  
**Tiwas baseline:** *Tiwas—Alpha-Playtest-Corpus-2026-09-01.md*, version 1.0  
**Assessment purpose:** Determine which Tiwas systems can currently support playtesting and which systems must be completed before the adventure can function as a complete Tiwas benchmark.

***

# 1. Executive Summary

*Beyond the Vale of Madness* is a suitable practical benchmark for Tiwas because it exercises more than ordinary skill resolution. Although it is a relatively short solo adventure, it assumes systems for character capability, exploration, environmental hazards, climbing, fatigue, equipment, encumbrance, fear, combat, tactical positioning, damage, injury, conditions, creatures, and death. [Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS](Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS.pdf)

Tiwas can already support the adventure’s **basic resolution layer**. Ordinary GURPS skill and attribute rolls can be replaced by the Tiwas Core Test without creating a second resolution engine. Tiwas also has usable foundations for attributes, skills, physical and mental resources, opposed contests, and hazard-related Location Index generation. 

However, Tiwas is not yet ready for a complete mechanical playtest of the adventure without temporary rulings. The principal blockers are:

- Combat procedure.
- Tactical movement and action order.
- Damage, armour, injury, and death.
- Fatigue and Physical Energy interpretation.
- Equipment, weapons, shields, and encumbrance.
- Creature construction.
- Conditions.
- Complete S-3 effect contents.

### Overall finding

> **Tiwas is Playtestable Now for a restricted exploration-and-resolution test, and Playtestable with Adaptation Mapping for several hazard and mental-resolution functions. It is not yet fully playtestable as a complete mechanical adaptation because the adventure exposes unresolved combat, injury, fatigue, equipment, and adversary systems.**

The adventure therefore provides a useful development diagnostic, but the result is not a binary “ready/not ready” outcome. Tiwas has a functioning core test architecture while still lacking several interconnected procedures required for a complete adventure.

***

# 2. Audit Objective and Method

## 2.1 Objective

This audit answers:

> Which systems required by *Beyond the Vale of Madness* are currently available in Tiwas, which can be supported through adaptation mapping, and which unresolved Tiwas systems prevent a complete playtest?

The purpose is not to reproduce GURPS procedures. The assessment instead asks:

1. What mechanical function does the adventure require?
2. Does Tiwas already provide that function?
3. If so, is the Tiwas mechanic authoritative and operational?
4. If not, is the problem an adventure-specific mapping task or a Tiwas design gap?

## 2.2 Source authority

The adventure PDF is treated as authoritative for what the adventure uses or assumes. The Tiwas Alpha Playtest Corpus is treated as authoritative for the dated baseline supplied for this assessment.

The corpus explicitly states that it is a one-off, table-ready compilation rather than a new canonical rules document. It preserves the distinction between:

- Canonical / Locked rules.
- Non-canonical designer rulings.
- Draft-pending material.
- Open items.
- Confirmed-closed items.

Only the first two categories are presented as table-ready mechanics in the corpus. 

## 2.3 Readiness classifications

| Classification | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Playtestable Now** | Tiwas already provides sufficient operational mechanics. |
| **Adaptation Mapping Required** | The underlying Tiwas function exists, but an adventure-specific mapping, statistic, or content decision must be authored. |
| **Design-Stage Dependency** | Tiwas has a recognised direction or subsystem, but it is not sufficiently complete or authoritative for dependable use. |
| **Missing Subsystem** | No adequate Tiwas procedure is currently established. |
| **Adventure Content Only** | Fictional, structural, or module-specific material rather than a Tiwas system. |

A result may be “playtestable” in a deliberately provisional alpha test while still being unsuitable as evidence that the underlying subsystem is complete.

***

# 3. Source Adventure Mechanical Inventory

## 3.1 Adventure structure

The adventure is a solo, numbered-paragraph “Choose Your Path” scenario. The player reads a paragraph, makes choices, records discovered bold-faced items, and proceeds to another numbered entry. It is presented as an introductory GURPS Fantasy or Dungeon Fantasy adventure and assumes either a 150-point fantasy character or one of two pregenerated characters. [Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS](Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS.pdf)

The following are **adventure procedures or content**, not Tiwas subsystems:

- Numbered paragraph navigation.
- Branching choices.
- Castle, caves, snow, and supernatural setting.
- Enfys and other named characters.
- The Castle of Madness.
- The ice troll and other fictional entities as named inhabitants.
- The adventure’s specific treasure and item placements.
- Flags such as writing “AMBUSHED” on the character sheet.
- The module’s paragraph references and alternate routes.

These still require adaptation work, but they do not indicate missing Tiwas rules by themselves.

## 3.2 Mechanical requirements identified

| Requirement | Adventure use |
|---|---|
| Character capability | The adventure assumes a fantasy character with attributes, skills, equipment, health, fatigue, and combat capability. |
| Ordinary tests | Will, DX, ST, Climbing, and other checks are explicitly called for. |
| Difficulty modifiers | Examples include DX-5 and encumbrance-based penalties. |
| Exploration | The character searches ruins, caves, doors, tunnels, weapons, and concealed areas. |
| Perception | The character notices routes, creatures, openings, unusual objects, and environmental details. |
| Climbing | The character climbs a dangerous cliff or castle approach. |
| Falling | Failed climbing may cause crushing damage. |
| Environmental exposure | Snow, freezing winds, darkness, and extreme cold are persistent threats. |
| Physical exertion | Digging and movement reduce fatigue. |
| Fatigue depletion | The adventure subtracts FP and states that reaching zero causes collapse. |
| Equipment | Torches, cloaks, weapons, shields, armour, and recovered objects matter. |
| Encumbrance | Encumbrance modifies climbing. |
| Weapon skills | The mace requires Axe/Mace skill. |
| Weapon statistics | The mace has damage, a strength requirement, and weight. |
| Combat | The player may attack creatures, including an ice troll. |
| Tactical combat | The adventure provides positions, adjacency, a map, and tactical alternatives. |
| Action order | Ambush conditions affect who moves first. |
| Damage | Crushing and cutting damage are used, including falling damage. |
| Armour | Soft armour and shield/equipment protection are referenced. |
| Fear and mental resistance | A Will roll modified by Fearlessness may be required. |
| Opposed interaction | Creature and hazard encounters may require opposed resolution. |
| Conditions | Fear, exhaustion, injury, collapse, and possible incapacitation are represented. |
| Death | Severe injury or collapse can end the adventure. |
| Recovery | Persistent HP and FP consequences must be tracked between paragraphs. |
| Creature statistics | The ice troll must be represented as an opponent. |
| Magic | The adventure supports a pregenerated character using GURPS Magic, creating a possible magic-system dependency. |

The PDF evidence directly shows Will, DX, Climbing, ST, falling damage, fatigue-point depletion, weapon statistics, tactical combat, and the ice-troll encounter. [Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS](Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS.pdf)

# 4. System-by-System Tiwas Compatibility Assessment

## 4.1 Core resolution and character capability

| Adventure requirement | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Classification | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary skill rolls | Tiwas uses a d100 roll-under test. A test succeeds when the roll is at or below Skill, with a universal roll of 100 failure. | Canonical / Locked, DEC-001 | **Playtestable Now** | Low | Map each adventure action to a Tiwas skill. |
| Core test procedure | Tiwas requires the nine-step Core Test Transaction, including resource cost, overflow, failure XP, failed doubles, and recovery. | Canonical / Locked, DEC-006 and related core rules | **Playtestable Now** | Medium | Ensure every adapted test uses the Core Test rather than a GURPS substitute. |
| Physical and mental abilities | Tiwas has 24 Body and Mind attributes and associated Tier-1 skills such as Might, Agility, Reflexes, Quickness, Willpower, Perception, Resolve, and Composure. | Canonical / Locked, DEC-003 to DEC-005 | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Medium | Define the adventure’s mapping from ST, DX, Will, and Perception to Tiwas skills. |
| Untrained fallback | The adventure allows DX-5 when the character lacks Climbing. | GURPS adventure procedure; no confirmed Tiwas equivalent identified | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Medium | Establish whether untrained actions use a related Tiwas skill, attribute, or fixed penalty. |
| Difficulty modifiers | The adventure uses DX-5 and other penalties. | Adventure requirement; complete universal Tiwas modifier policy not established in available evidence | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Medium | Define how penalties modify the Core Test without violating the Core Test architecture. |
| Resource cost | Every Tiwas test costs the natural roll from the relevant resource domain. | Canonical / Locked | **Playtestable Now** | Low | Decide whether this cost applies unchanged to all mapped adventure checks. |

Tiwas’s core test is a strong compatibility point. The main unresolved issue is not resolution itself, but mapping GURPS attributes, untrained checks, and modifiers into the Tiwas architecture.

## 4.2 Exploration and environmental hazards

| Adventure requirement | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Classification | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Searching and noticing features | Standard tests can resolve investigation and perception. | Canonical core plus attribute/skill framework | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Low | Assign relevant Tiwas skills. |
| Hidden doors and traps | DEC-037 expressly covers environmental hazards, obstacles, and examples such as Spot Trap. | Non-canonical designer ruling, ruled | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Low | Create the specific trap or door content. |
| Climbing | A failed Climbing or physical-risk test can use the Tiwas Core Test. | Canonical core; hazard-location ruling | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Medium | Define the Tiwas Climbing skill and consequence severity. |
| Hazard failure provenance | A failed hazard test supplies the digits for Zero-Step Location Index generation. | Non-canonical designer ruling, DEC-037 | **Playtestable Now** for the ruled alpha baseline | Medium | Confirm use in the module’s specific failures. |
| Extended physical tests | DEC-039 states that the final roll of an Extended Test governs Location Index generation. | Non-canonical designer ruling, ruled | **Design-Stage Dependency** unless the adventure is treated as single-roll | Medium | Determine whether any adventure sequence qualifies as an Extended Test. |
| Extreme cold | Systemic threats such as extreme temperature bypass Location Index and apply direct HP/Conditions. | Non-canonical designer ruling, DEC-037 | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | High | Define exposure frequency, severity, and recovery. |
| Falling | The adventure applies \(1d-1\) crushing damage after a failed climb. | GURPS adventure procedure | **Design-Stage Dependency** | High | Establish Tiwas falling damage and physical-consequence procedure. |
| Darkness and torches | The adventure assumes torch use and limited cave visibility. | Adventure requirement; no complete Tiwas light subsystem established in evidence | **Missing Subsystem** or design-stage dependency | Medium | Define visibility, torch duration, and darkness effects if mechanically tested. |
| Navigation and route-finding | Narrative exploration and ordinary perception tests can support route choices. | Core resolution available | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Low | Author any required navigation tests. |

DEC-037 is especially relevant because it provides a direct mechanical bridge between failed environmental tests and physical consequences. It also explicitly treats extreme temperature as a systemic threat rather than a location-indexed injury. 

## 4.3 Fatigue, energy, and persistence

| Adventure requirement | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Classification | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Exertion costs | Tiwas has Physical Energy and Energy Regen. | Canonical / Locked, DEC-004 | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | High | Decide whether GURPS FP is replaced by Physical Energy. |
| Fixed fatigue loss | Digging subtracts 1 FP. | Adventure procedure | **Design-Stage Dependency** | High | Define whether fixed exertion costs are permitted under the Core Test architecture. |
| Zero-resource collapse | The adventure states that reaching 0 FP causes collapse. | Adventure procedure; Tiwas zero-energy consequence not established in supplied evidence | **Missing Subsystem** | High | Define zero Physical Energy consequences. |
| Repeated resource tracking | The solo structure requires resources to persist between paragraphs. | Core resources exist, but adventure-state procedures are not fully specified | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Medium | Create a character-state tracking procedure. |
| Recovery | Tiwas includes Energy Regen and recovery as the final Core Test step. | Canonical / Locked | **Playtestable Now** for test-linked recovery | Medium | Define between-scene and injury recovery. |

The existence of Physical Energy does not automatically make GURPS Fatigue Points available in Tiwas. The replacement relationship must be explicitly decided.

## 4.4 Equipment, weapons, armour, and encumbrance

| Adventure requirement | Tiwas capability | Authority/status | Classification | Blocking significance | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inventory | The adventure expects players to record discovered bold-faced items. | Adventure procedure | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Low | Use a Tiwas inventory record. |
| Weapon skill | The recovered mace requires Axe/Mace skill. | Adventure content plus GURPS rule | **Design-Stage Dependency** | High | Define Tiwas weapon-skill categories. |
| Weapon damage | The mace deals \(sw+2\) crushing damage. | GURPS weapon statistic | **Design-Stage Dependency** | High | Define Tiwas damage values and remove GURPS swing notation. |
| Strength requirement | Mace requires ST 12. | GURPS weapon statistic | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Medium | Map to a Tiwas physical-power requirement. |
| Weight | Mace weighs 5 lb. | GURPS equipment statistic | **Design-Stage Dependency** | Medium | Define Tiwas weight and carrying model. |
| Shields | A medium shield is found and used as equipment. | Adventure content; Tiwas defensive function not established in evidence | **Design-Stage Dependency** | High | Define shield protection or defensive effects. |
| Armour | Falling damage references soft armour protection. | GURPS combat/equipment procedure | **Design-Stage Dependency** | High | Define armour reduction or injury mitigation. |
| Encumbrance | Climbing rolls receive a penalty per encumbrance level. | GURPS procedure | **Missing Subsystem** or design-stage dependency | High | Establish encumbrance levels and their effects. |
| Torch | Torch provides light and heat in caves. | Adventure content with mechanical implications | **Adaptation Mapping Required** | Medium | Define duration and visibility effects. |

This is one of the clearest areas where an ordinary Tiwas skill roll is insufficient. A standard test can determine whether the character attempts or uses an item successfully, but weapon damage, armour, weight, shields, and encumbrance require additional systems.

The ice-troll encounter is the principal full-playtest blocker. The adventure does not merely ask whether the character succeeds at an attack; it assumes an integrated combat model with movement, positioning, attack order, damage, and creature behaviour. # 6. Missing / Design-Stage Dependencies

## 6.1 Critical blockers

### Combat resolution

The adventure’s combat cannot be evaluated using the Core Test alone. A complete combat procedure must specify:

- Attack declaration.
- Attack skill.
- Defence or opposing test.
- Turn/action order.
- Movement.
- Range and adjacency.
- Tactical positioning.
- Retreat.
- Damage application.
- Creature behaviour.
- Incapacitation.

**Status:** Design-stage dependency.

### Damage and injury

The adventure requires crushing, cutting, and falling damage, as well as armour interaction and minimum-damage handling. Tiwas currently exposes HP and Location Index foundations, but not a complete evidenced damage-to-injury procedure.

**Status:** Design-stage dependency.

### Conditions

The adventure needs at least Wounded, exhausted, frightened, unconscious, and dead or dying states. The corpus confirms a Conditions concept, but it also states that the contents of several gated S-3 tiers remain incompletely enumerated. 

**Status:** Design-stage dependency.

### Fatigue and Physical Energy

The adventure’s FP rules cannot be imported directly. A Tiwas-specific decision is needed regarding fixed exertion costs, zero-energy collapse, and recovery.

**Status:** Design-stage dependency.

### Equipment and encumbrance

The adventure uses weapon skill, weapon damage, strength requirements, weight, shields, armour, torches, and encumbrance penalties. These cannot be reduced to ordinary skill tests.

**Status:** Encumbrance is a missing or unresolved subsystem; equipment is a design-stage dependency.

### Creature construction

The ice troll requires a repeatable Tiwas representation. A one-off improvised stat block would permit a narrow demonstration but would not prove that adversary construction is ready.

**Status:** Design-stage dependency.

## 6.2 Non-blocking or low-blocking gaps

The following do not prevent a restricted exploration test:

- Torch duration.
- Detailed navigation.
- Exact fear-condition effects.
- Optional magic.
- Precise treasure statistics.
- Full tactical combat, provided the combat encounter is excluded or explicitly marked provisional.

***

# 7. Adventure Path Dependency Analysis

## 7.1 Opening approach and snow route

The opening route requires travel through cold, snow, darkness, and environmental danger. It may include perception, investigation, and Will-related choices.

**Tiwas result:** Mostly testable through the Core Test and Mind/Body skills. Extreme-temperature consequences and long-term fatigue remain unresolved.

**Readiness:** Restricted playtest possible.

## 7.2 Castle approach and climbing route

The cliff or castle approach requires Climbing, encumbrance penalties, and falling consequences. The adventure explicitly uses Climbing or DX-5 and applies falling damage on failure. [Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS](Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS.pdf)

**Tiwas result:** The test itself is compatible. Hazard-location provenance is supported by DEC-037. Falling damage, encumbrance, armour, and injury are not complete.

**Readiness:** Testable only with documented temporary substitutions.

## 7.3 Cave and tunnel route

The cave route uses torchlight, perception, hidden passages, equipment discovery, movement, and potential creature encounters.

**Tiwas result:** Exploration can be tested. Light, equipment, movement, and creature procedures require mapping or further design.

**Readiness:** Exploration route is testable; creature confrontation is not fully supported.

## 7.4 Ice-troll encounter

The ice-troll encounter is the strongest readiness test. It includes:

- Combat choice.
- Tactical combat.
- Starting positions.
- Adjacency.
- Ambush state.
- First movement.
- Creature tactics.
- Weapon attacks.
- Damage.
- Possible escape or death.

The adventure states that the troll rushes toward the character and provides different starting positions depending on whether the character has recorded “AMBUSHED.” [Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS](Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS.pdf)

**Tiwas result:** The encounter cannot currently function as a complete Tiwas combat benchmark without provisional combat, damage, creature, and condition rules.

**Readiness:** Not fully playtestable.

## 7.5 Optional magic-character route

The optional advanced character uses GURPS Magic.

**Tiwas result:** This tests a Tiwas magic system rather than the adventure’s general readiness. If magic is not already established in the Tiwas baseline, this route should be excluded from the first benchmark.

**Readiness:** Not required for the core adventure benchmark.

# 8. Tiwas Readiness Assessment

## 8.1 Readiness by architectural layer

| Layer | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Primary resolution architecture | Ready. The canonical d100 Core Test is sufficient for ordinary tests. |
| Attribute and skill foundation | Ready, subject to adventure-specific mapping. |
| Resource architecture | Partially ready. HP, MP, Physical Energy, and regeneration exist, but fatigue interpretation is unresolved. |
| Hazard resolution | Partially ready. The S-2/S-4 location framework provides a usable basis. |
| Opposed resolution | Partially ready. S-1 is available, but its use in combat requires mapping. |
| Effect resolution | Not fully ready. S-3 structure exists, but relevant gated contents remain incomplete. |
| Combat architecture | Not ready for complete adventure playtesting. |
| Damage and injury | Not ready. |
| Conditions | Not ready for dependable use. |
| Equipment and encumbrance | Not ready. |
| Adversary construction | Not demonstrated as ready. |
| Magic | Not required for the core benchmark and not evidenced as ready. |
| Adventure-state tracking | Adaptable but requires a practical worksheet or procedure. |

## 8.2 Quantitative interpretation

This audit should not be reduced to a simple percentage because the systems have unequal blocking significance. A missing torch-duration rule is not equivalent to a missing combat-and-injury engine.

A more useful interpretation is:

- **Core test readiness:** High.
- **Exploration readiness:** Moderate to high.
- **Hazard readiness:** Moderate.
- **Mental-test readiness:** Moderate to high.
- **Combat readiness:** Low.
- **Physical-consequence readiness:** Low.
- **Equipment/readiness:** Low.
- **Complete adventure readiness:** Low to moderate, depending on whether provisional systems are permitted.

***

# 9. Development Priorities Exposed by the Adventure

## Priority 1: Complete the combat consequence chain

The first priority should be a connected package rather than isolated rules:

1. Attack.
2. Defence.
3. Position and movement.
4. Damage.
5. Armour.
6. Injury.
7. Conditions.
8. Incapacitation.
9. Death and recovery.

This is the most important dependency because the ice-troll encounter exercises nearly all of these systems at once.

## Priority 2: Establish the physical resource model

Resolve:

- Whether Physical Energy replaces FP.
- Whether fixed costs such as “subtract 1 FP” are permitted.
- What zero Physical Energy does.
- How exertion differs from Core Test resource cost.
- How extreme temperature drains or affects resources.
- How energy recovers between scenes.

## Priority 3: Establish equipment and encumbrance

Create a minimum operational equipment layer covering:

- Weapons.
- Weapon skills.
- Damage values.
- Strength or Might requirements.
- Weight.
- Shields.
- Armour.
- Torches.
- Encumbrance levels.

## Priority 4: Complete conditions and S-3 effects

The adventure requires conditions even if the initial prototype uses only a small set. Define at minimum:

- Wounded.
- Exhausted.
- Frightened.
- Impaired.
- Unconscious.
- Dying/dead.
- Immobilised or restrained, if relevant to combat.

The corpus specifically warns that the structure of several S-3 gated effect tiers is ruled while their contents are not fully enumerated. 

## Priority 5: Define adversary construction

Use the ice troll as a test case for a general creature format, not merely as a one-off exception. The format should include:

- Attributes.
- Skills.
- HP and resources.
- Movement.
- Attack and defence.
- Damage.
- Conditions.
- Special abilities.
- Tactics.

## Priority 6: Create an adventure readiness worksheet

Future module audits should record each requirement using the same fields:

- Adventure page/paragraph.
- Mechanical function.
- Tiwas subsystem.
- Tiwas status.
- Readiness classification.
- Blocking significance.
- Adaptation decision.
- Playtest observation.

This will make future adventures comparable as readiness benchmarks.

***

# 10. Conclusions

*Beyond the Vale of Madness* confirms that Tiwas already has a usable core resolution architecture. Standard GURPS tests can be replaced by the Tiwas Core Test, and the attribute, skill, resource, opposed-contest, and hazard-location foundations are sufficient for a restricted exploration playtest. 

The adventure also demonstrates that a Core Test is not a complete game system. Its combat, falling, fatigue, weapon, shield, armour, encumbrance, injury, condition, creature, and death requirements expose several unresolved Tiwas dependencies.

### Final determination

| Question | Finding |
|---|---|
| Can the adventure be used to test ordinary Tiwas resolution now? | Yes. |
| Can its exploration and branching structure be tested now? | Yes. |
| Can environmental hazards be tested? | Yes, with adaptation mapping and provisional consequence handling. |
| Can fear and Will tests be tested? | Yes, for basic mental tests. |
| Can the ice-troll combat be fully tested? | No, not without provisional combat and injury rules. |
| Can the entire adventure be run without inventing mechanics? | No. |
| Is the adventure useful as a Tiwas readiness benchmark? | Yes. |
| What is the most important development target? | The integrated combat–damage–conditions–resource package. |

> **Readiness verdict:** Tiwas is currently suitable for a **restricted exploration and Core Test playtest** of *Beyond the Vale of Madness*. It is not yet suitable for a **complete mechanical playtest** of the adventure. The adventure’s most valuable diagnostic contribution is showing that Tiwas must next complete the systems connecting action resolution to physical consequences.

# 12. Explicit Assumptions and Unresolved Questions

## 12.1 Explicit assumptions

1. Every GURPS skill or attribute roll is converted into an ordinary Tiwas Core Test, as instructed.
2. GURPS ST, DX, Will, and Fearlessness are not imported as Tiwas mechanics.
3. Physical Energy is treated as a possible FP replacement only for analysis; this is not a confirmed Tiwas ruling.
4. Tiwas’s Location Index procedures are treated as available for alpha playtesting where the corpus identifies them as ruled.
5. Non-canonical designer rulings remain non-canonical and are not presented as locked Tiwas rules.
6. The optional GURPS Magic character is excluded from the minimum readiness determination.
7. Where the supplied evidence does not establish a complete operational rule, the assessment is conservative and classifies it as design-stage or missing rather than assuming a GM improvisation is a system.

## 12.2 Unresolved questions requiring designer decisions

1. Which Tiwas skills should replace GURPS ST, DX, Will, and Perception in this adventure?
2. How should an untrained action such as GURPS DX-5 be expressed in Tiwas?
3. Is there a universal Tiwas difficulty-modifier rule?
4. Does Physical Energy replace GURPS FP?
5. What happens when Physical Energy reaches zero?
6. How are fixed exertion costs handled under the Core Test architecture?
7. What is the complete Tiwas attack-and-defence procedure?
8. How are crushing, cutting, and falling damage represented?
9. How do armour and shields reduce or redirect damage?
10. What conditions are currently operational?
11. What are the thresholds for unconsciousness and death?
12. How are creatures constructed?
13. How are initiative, ambush, movement, adjacency, and tactical range resolved?
14. Which S-3 effects are available in combat, and what are their exact contents?
15. What minimum magic rules are required before the optional magical character can be used?

These questions are not recommendations to improvise during the audit. They are the specific design decisions exposed by using the adventure as a readiness benchmark.
```

## btvmadness-adapt-report-recallAI-1.md

```markdown
# Tiwas Adventure Readiness Audit: *Beyond the Vale of Madness*

## 1. Executive Summary
This audit evaluates the **Tiwas TTRPG Alpha Corpus (2026-09-01)** against the mechanical requirements of the GURPS adventure *Beyond the Vale of Madness*. The audit finds that while the **Core Test Transaction (DEC-006)** and **Universal Opposed Contest (S-1)** are fully capable of resolving the adventure's primary challenges, the project faces a critical blockage in **S-12 (Creature/NPC Content)** and **S-3 (Effect Enumeration)**. 

**Key Finding:** A "bare-bones" playtest is possible now, but it requires the GM to manually author content for every monster and environmental condition, as Tiwas currently lacks the "Content Layer" to support its "System Layer."

---

## 2. Audit Objective and Method
*   **Objective:** Use *Beyond the Vale of Madness* as a benchmark to identify which Tiwas systems are playtest-ready and which are blocking development.
*   **Method:** 
    1.  Inventory every mechanical demand in the GURPS PDF.
    2.  Map those demands to Tiwas Canonical Rules (Part A) or Ruled Non-canonical Subsystems (Part B).
    3.  Classify readiness based on the delta between adventure requirements and Tiwas capabilities.

---

## 3. Source Adventure Mechanical Inventory
The adventure assumes the following mechanical capabilities:
*   **Resolution:** Success/Failure checks for Skills (Lockpicking, Climbing, Stealth) and Attributes (DX, Will, ST).
*   **Combat:** Tactical movement, hit points, damage types (crushing, cutting, corrosive), and active defense (Dodge/Parry).
*   **Environment:** Fatigue/Exhaustion tracking, hypothermia/cold damage, and falling damage.
*   **Status Effects:** Fear (Fright Checks), Darkness (vision penalties), and Wounds (localized injury).
*   **NPCs:** Stat blocks for Ice Trolls and Blood Men, including unique abilities (Regeneration, Blood Seep).
*   **Economy:** Treasure values and merchant bartering.

---

## 4. System-by-System Tiwas Compatibility Assessment

| Adventure Requirement | Tiwas Capability | Authority / Status | Readiness Classification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Skill/Attribute Checks** | Core Test Transaction (DEC-006) | Canonical / Locked | **Playtestable Now** |
| **Opposed Contests** | S-1 Universal Contest (DEC-013) | Canonical / Locked | **Playtestable Now** |
| **Hit Location** | Zero-Step Location Index (DEC-014) | Canonical / Locked | **Playtestable Now** |
| **Armor/Shields** | Armor Tags/Traits (DEC-058) | Non-canonical Ruling | **Playtestable Now** |
| **Active Defense** | Active Defense Mitigation (DEC-044) | Non-canonical Ruling | **Playtestable Now** |
| **Environmental Damage** | S-2/S-4 Provenance Rule (DEC-037) | Non-canonical Ruling | **Playtestable Now** |
| **Extended Tasks** | Margin-accumulation (DEC-067) | Non-canonical Ruling | **Playtestable Now** |
| **Monster Stats** | Abbreviated Stat-blocks (DEC-076) | Non-canonical Ruling | **Adaptation Mapping Required** |
| **Fear/Darkness** | S-8 Difficulty Modifiers (DEC-063) | Non-canonical Ruling | **Adaptation Mapping Required** |
| **Specific Status Effects** | S-3 Effect Menu (DEC-023) | Non-canonical Ruling | **Design-Stage Dependency** |
| **Creature Templates** | S-12 Content Authoring (DEC-077) | Open / Content | **Missing Subsystem** |

---

## 5. Playtestability Matrix

| System | Playtestable? | Blocking Significance | Remaining Work |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Engine** | **YES** | Low | None. |
| **Combat** | **YES** | Low | Requires GM to assign "Tags" to weapons/armor. |
| **Exploration** | **YES** | Low | Requires GM to set "Difficulty Tiers" (S-8). |
| **Monsters** | **PARTIAL** | **HIGH** | **S-12 is empty.** No pre-made Ice Troll exists. |
| **Magic** | **NO** | Medium | S-3 gated effects for spells are not enumerated. |
| **Survival** | **YES** | Low | Uses DEC-037 (failed roll → location injury). |

---

## 6. Missing / Design-Stage Dependencies
### 6.1 S-12 Creature/NPC Content (Missing)
The adventure requires an **Ice Troll** (ST 15, HP 15, DR 2, Regeneration). 
*   **Tiwas Gap:** While DEC-076 allows for simplified stats, there is no "Bestiary" or "Template" system. 
*   **Impact:** The GM must invent the Troll's 24 attributes or simplified equivalents from scratch.

### 6.2 S-3 Effect Enumeration (Design-Stage)
The adventure uses **Fright Checks** (#2, #38, #58) and **Darkness** (#7).
*   **Tiwas Gap:** DEC-023 defines the *structure* of the Effect menu, but the specific "Fear" or "Blindness" conditions are not defined.
*   **Impact:** The GM must decide the mechanical penalty for "Fear" (e.g., -20 to effective Skill) without system guidance.

---

## 7. Adventure Path Dependency Analysis
*   **Shortest Path (Cave → Troll → Exit):** Requires S-1 (Combat), S-12 (Troll Stats), and S-4 (Wounds). **Blocked by S-12.**
*   **Exploration Path (Castle → Traps → Loot):** Requires S-8 (Difficulty), S-9 (Extended Tests for Lockpicking), and S-5 (Armor). **Playtestable Now.**
*   **Social Path (Rescuing Jrak Kul):** Requires S-11 (Healing/Rest) and S-1 (Opposed Merchant rolls). **Playtestable Now.**

---

## 8. Tiwas Readiness Assessment
Tiwas is **System-Ready** but **Content-Empty**. 
The "Mechanical Engine" (Parts A & B of the Corpus) is surprisingly complete for this adventure. The "Universal Opposed Contest" (S-1) and "Active Defense" (S-6) cover 90% of the tactical needs. The "Extended Test" (S-9) perfectly handles the multi-step digging and climbing sequences.

The failure point is **S-12**. Without a standardized way to represent a "Monster," the system cannot be playtested as a standalone product; it remains a toolkit for a GM who is also a game designer.

---

## 9. Development Priorities Exposed by the Adventure
1.  **Priority 1: S-12 Template Authoring.** Create a "Standard Humanoid" and "Large Beast" template to allow for rapid NPC conversion.
2.  **Priority 2: S-3 Condition Enumeration.** Define a standard set of 5–10 common conditions (Fear, Blind, Prone, Bleeding) to populate the gated tiers.
3.  **Priority 3: S-5 Tag Library.** Create a list of standard weapon/armor Tags (e.g., *Reach*, *Heavy*, *Deflective*) so players don't have to invent them during character creation.

---

## 10. Conclusions
*Beyond the Vale of Madness* is an excellent benchmark for Tiwas because it relies heavily on **environmental pressure** and **localized injury**, both of which Tiwas handles natively via DEC-037 and S-4. 

**Final Verdict:** You can playtest this adventure in Tiwas **today**, provided the GM accepts the burden of "Content Authoring" for the monsters and specific status effects. The core math and resolution logic will not break.

---

## 11. Source and Evidence Register
*   **Core Resolution:** DEC-001 through DEC-016 (Canonical).
*   **Combat/Defense:** DEC-044 through DEC-050 (S-6).
*   **Wounds/Location:** DEC-032 through DEC-042 (S-4).
*   **Difficulty:** DEC-063 through DEC-066 (S-8).
*   **Extended Tests:** DEC-067 through DEC-070 (S-9/10).

---

## 12. Explicit Assumptions / Unresolved Questions
*   **Assumption:** GURPS "Fatigue Points" (FP) are mapped to Tiwas **Physical Energy** (bep+bes+bee).
*   **Assumption:** GURPS "Damage Resistance" (DR) is mapped to Tiwas **Armor Tags** (S-5).
*   **Unresolved:** How to handle the "Regeneration" of the Ice Troll without a Tiwas "Healing-over-time" mechanic (S-11 is currently Rest-based only).
*   **Unresolved:** The specific "Shatterproof" enchantment on the Glass Dagger (#24) has no Tiwas equivalent; it must be treated as a narrative Tag.
```

```markdown
# Tiwas Adventure Readiness Audit — *Beyond the Vale of Madness* (GURPS) Benchmark

## 1. Executive Summary

*Beyond the Vale of Madness* is a short GURPS Dungeon Fantasy solo/GM adventure built on
four core attributes (ST/DX/IQ/HT), skill defaults, situational modifiers, GURPS hit
location, Fright Checks, and a character-point advancement award at completion. Tiwas'
Core Test Transaction (DEC-006), S-1 Opposed Contest, and the S-2/S-4 Location-Index +
Wound chain already cover the *structural* demands of ordinary skill tests, falls, combat
resolution, and localized injury — these are **Playtestable Now** or **Adaptation Mapping
Required** rather than blocked.

Three categories of adventure-mechanical demand are **not currently coverable** by any
Ruled or Locked Tiwas material:

1. **Skill/attribute defaults** (e.g. "IQ‑2 if you do not have the skill," "DX‑8 or ST‑8
   if you do not have the skill") — no Tiwas mechanism exists for testing an
   attribute/related-skill in place of an absent Skill.
2. **Fright Check / sanity-adjacent resolution** — thematically central to a "Castle of
   Madness" adventure, and entirely absent from the Tiwas ruleset.
3. **Fall/impact damage magnitude and the ST/Encumbrance/Basic Lift/Basic Move chargen
   layer** — Reserved (DEC-015) and not yet built; Tiwas' Movement Speed formula does not
   substitute for GURPS' Basic Move/Encumbrance interaction, and Tiwas has no equivalent
   of Advantages/Disadvantages/Perks/Quirks or Reaction Modifiers.

The single largest blocking factor for **full mechanical fidelity** is not combat (S-1
through S-6 already form a workable Core-Test-based combat loop) but the **absence of a
skill-default / untrained-attribute-substitution rule** and the **absence of any
fear/sanity subsystem**, both of which this specific adventure invokes repeatedly and
which no open Tiwas investigation currently addresses.

Everything else — treasure, NPC content, the branching paragraph structure, named
locations — is **Adventure Content Only** and requires authored adaptation, not new Tiwas
mechanics.

---

## 2. Audit Objective and Method

**Objective.** Determine, system by system, whether Tiwas TTRPG as currently Ruled/Locked
can support a full-fidelity playtest of *Beyond the Vale of Madness*, and where it cannot,
identify precisely which Tiwas subsystem is responsible.

**Method.**
1. Inventory every mechanical demand actually present in the adventure text (not merely
   those on its shortest path) — attribute/skill rolls, modifiers, defaults, damage,
   combat implications, character-sheet fields, and the completion-award mechanic.
2. Map each demand to its **required function** (what the game system must accomplish),
   per the mandated "function first, not GURPS procedure" adaptation philosophy.
3. Cross-reference that function against the Tiwas Alpha-Playtest Corpus (2026-09-01),
   distinguishing Canonical/Locked (Part A), Non-canonical designer ruling (Part B), Open/
   design-stage (Part C), and content-authoring items.
4. Classify each item under the five Readiness Categories defined in the tasking prompt.
5. Where the corpus is silent, the item is classified **Missing Subsystem** — silence is
   not treated as permission to invent a mechanic.

**Constraint compliance note.** No GURPS procedure (defaults, hit-location penalty table,
Fright Check, CP economy) is imported into Tiwas. Every ordinary GURPS skill/attribute
roll below is treated as an ordinary Tiwas Core Test per the tasking prompt's explicit
instruction, regardless of what GURPS mechanism originally resolved it.

---

## 3. Source Adventure Mechanical Inventory

Extracted directly from `Beyond-the-Vale-of-Madness-GURPS.md`. Picture-text OCR blocks are
decorative/illustrative scans and contain no extractable mechanical content beyond the
character-sheet layout captured separately below.

| # | Mechanical element | Adventure occurrence(s) |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Plain attribute test (DX roll) | Icy stairway descent (§~28 area); troll-avoidance peek (§31); pit jump (§55) |
| M2 | Skill test with situational modifier | Tracking roll **at +3** (§27) |
| M3 | Skill-or-attribute-default test | "Tracking roll at +3, or an **IQ-2** if you do not have the skill" (§27); "Climbing roll **at -3** (or **DX-8** or **ST-8** if you do not have the skill!)" (§35) |
| M4 | Skill test, no modifier, either-of-two-skills | "Search or Perception (Vision) roll" (§30); "First Aid or PhysiciAn roll" (§37) |
| M5 | Fall/impact damage on failure | "Take 1d-2 cr damage" (stairs; §28 area); "you take 1d-4 cr damage from the fall" (§55 pit) |
| M6 | Fright Check | "You must make a Fright Check at -2 (see p. B360)!" on discovering a corpse (§58) |
| M7 | Implied melee combat vs. a hostile creature | Ice troll encounter — "You slam your weapon again and again against the ice" (§26 area); troll described as actively hunting the character (§31–32, §37 recap) |
| M8 | Character core attributes | ST, DX, IQ, HT (four-attribute chargen block on the character sheet) |
| M9 | Secondary/derived stats | HP, Will, Per, FP, Basic Lift, Basic Speed, Basic Move |

| M13 | Skills list with numeric Level | Character-sheet field; adventure text names Tracking, Search, Perception, First Aid, Physician, Climbing as in-use skills |
| M14 | Languages (Spoken/Written) | Character-sheet field |
| M15 | Hand Weapons table | Damage / Reach / Parry / Notes / Cost / Weight |
| M16 | Ranged Weapons table | Damage / Acc / Range / RoF / Shots / ST / Bulk / Rcl / LC / Notes / Cost / Weight |
```
