- **Agreement:** Among the 6 reports that address it, all agree Tiwas has no explicit default/substitution rule.

**Status / Tiwas baseline:** S-3 has a Condition tier in its menu structure (Ruled), but the specific Condition contents are explicitly not table-ready (Part C.3 of the corpus).

**Reporting LLMs:** 23 of 25 reports address this explicitly.

**Per-report positions:** Universal agreement that the Condition tier structure is Ruled but the contents are not enumerated. Classification varies between Design-Stage Dependency and Missing Subsystem.

**Representative quotes:**

- ChatGPT 5.5-high: *"The Tiwas corpus explicitly places conditions outside the locked Core and S-3 has only a structural Condition tier whose detailed contents remain incomplete."*
- Kimi K3: *"Conditions System — ⚠️ Design-Stage Dependency. Blocking: Low. The adventure's word-tracking (DARKNESS, AMBUSHED, RESCUER) is narrative, not mechanical."*
- Claude 5 Sonnet: *"The Tiwas corpus refers to Conditions and specifically 'Wounded,' but the supplied material says some gated effect contents remain incompletely enumerated."*

**Collated synthesis:**

- **Agreement:** Universal that the structure is Ruled and contents are not enumerated.
- **Unresolved:** None at the architectural level.
- **Coverage limitation:** 2 of 25 reports do not address this question.

---

### Tactical Combat / Action Economy / Time

**Status / Tiwas baseline:** Reserved per DEC-015. No Ruled subsystem for hex-based tactical combat, initiative, or action economy.

**Reporting LLMs:** 22 of 25 reports address this explicitly.

**Per-report positions:** Universal agreement that this is a Missing Subsystem. Most reports note that the adventure explicitly permits "trading blows" without tactical combat, so the blocker is partial rather than total.

**Representative quotes:**

- ChatGPT 5.6-1: *"Time is not optional if the full adventure is to be run faithfully as a Tiwas test... Readiness: 🔴 Design-stage dependency."*
- ChatGPT 5.5-high: *"The adventure's battle maps require meaningful positional play... Tiwas does not currently provide a sufficiently complete universal tactical action economy."*
- Mistral: *"Tactical combat is optional... If tactical combat is mandatory, this increases blocker priority."*

**Collated synthesis:**

- **Agreement:** Universal that the subsystem is Missing; universal that the adventure permits abstract combat as an alternative.
- **Unresolved:** None.
- **Coverage limitation:** 3 of 25 reports do not address this question.

---

### Damage Types / Damage Magnitude

**Status / Tiwas baseline:** Tiwas has HP and Overflow → HP. No Ruled subsystem for damage types (crushing, cutting, impaling, corrosive) or for a general damage-magnitude procedure independent of Overflow.

**Reporting LLMs:** 20 of 25 reports address this explicitly.

**Per-report positions:**

- **Kimi K3:** Flags as **Critical Design-Stage Dependency**. *"The S-3 Effect menu (DEC-023) defines Inflict Injury as 'HP-only' but provides no mechanism for determining the quantity of HP damage."*
- **ChatGPT 5.5-high, ChatGPT 5.6-1, ChatGPT 5.6-2, Grok 4.6-1, Grok 4.6-2, Muse Spark 1.1-1, Muse Spark 1.1-2, Claude 5 Sonnet:** Treat as Design-Stage Dependency or Adaptation Mapping Required.
- **Copilot 1, Copilot 365-1, Copilot 365-2, DeepSeek-V3, RecallAI:** Treat as Playtestable Now via base-tier Inflict Injury.
- **Mimo 2.5-1, Mimo 2.5-2:** Treat as Design-Stage Dependency.
- **Laguna S 2.1:** Treat as Playtestable Now for overflow-as-HP.
- **Gemini 3.6 Flash-1, Gemini 3.6 Flash-2:** Treat as Playtestable Now.
- **Perplexity 1, Perplexity 2:** Treat as Design-Stage Dependency.

**Collated synthesis:**

- **Agreement:** Universal that Tiwas has HP and Overflow → HP.
- **Disagreement:** **D10** — whether a separate damage-magnitude procedure is required.
- **Coverage limitation:** 5 of 25 reports do not address this question.

### Hit Location (GURPS Penalty-to-Hit Model)

**Status / Tiwas baseline:** Tiwas has Zero-Step Location Index (DEC-014) and anatomical mapping (DEC-041), but these are structurally different from GURPS's "declare a called shot at a penalty" model. DEC-014 §14.2 explicitly forecloses player-chosen targeting.

**Reporting LLMs:** 15 of 25 reports address this explicitly.

**Per-report positions:** Universal agreement that Tiwas's location system is structurally different from GURPS's. Most reports note that the adventure does not require called shots, so this is non-blocking for this specific adventure.

**Representative quotes:**

- Claude 5 Sonnet: *"Tiwas' location is a post-hoc read of the already-made roll, not a pre-declared targeting choice with its own penalty... Non-blocking for this specific adventure (no called shots occur in the supplied text)."*

**Collated synthesis:**

- **Agreement:** Universal that the systems are structurally different; universal that this is non-blocking for this adventure.
- **Unresolved:** None.
- **Coverage limitation:** 10 of 25 reports do not address this question.

## Section 6 — Guesses I Had to Make

| Item | Assumption / interpretation | Basis | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| What counts as a "system" | Each DEC or group of related DECs constituting a coherent mechanical area (e.g., S-1, S-2, S-3, etc.) plus cross-cutting areas not covered by a single DEC (e.g., Equipment, Magic, Fear). | Source reports consistently use this grouping. | High |
| What counts as a "subsystem" | A Ruled or Reserved mechanical area with its own DEC range (e.g., S-5 Armor = DEC-058–062). | Source reports consistently use this grouping. | High |
| Threshold distinguishing disagreement from complementary analysis | A disagreement is recorded only when two or more reports take materially different positions on a substantive question (readiness classification, blocking significance, or architectural conclusion). Different wording expressing the same conclusion is not manufactured into a disagreement. | Prompt instruction §2.5. | High |
| How ambiguous report wording was interpreted | Where a report's classification was ambiguous (e.g., "Playtestable Now with caveats"), the most conservative interpretation was used. | Prompt instruction §2.5. | Medium |
| Expected author identity | Taken from the attribution manifest; not inferred from writing style. | Attribution manifest. | High |
| Output/report metadata | Date = 2026-09-02 (current date); version = 1.0. | Prompt instruction §9. | High |
| Source boundaries | Only the three permitted sources were consulted; no external RPG knowledge was used. | Prompt instruction §6. | High |
| Interpretation of readiness labels | The five readiness categories (Playtestable Now, Adaptation Mapping Required, Design-Stage Dependency, Missing Subsystem, Adventure Content Only) were applied as defined in the source reports. | Source reports. | High |
| Missing or incomplete provenance | The producing-model identity is self-reported; no platform-metadata mechanism was available. | Prompt instruction §5. | High |
| Unresolved classification decision | Where a report did not explicitly classify a system, the classification was inferred from the report's overall treatment of that system. | Source reports. | Medium |
| Whether S-12 is a "system" or "content" | Treated as a system (S-12) with content-authoring dependencies, per the corpus's own treatment. | Corpus Part C.1. | High |
| Whether the adventure's optional tactical map is a system gap or adventure content | Treated as adventure content, per the adventure's explicit permission to "trade blows" without tactical combat. | Adventure text; 6 of 25 reports. | High |
| Whether GURPS FP maps to Tiwas Physical Energy | Treated as an adaptation decision, not a system gap; the mapping is not confirmed by any Tiwas ruling. | 21 of 25 reports. | High |
| Whether the adventure's "gain 2 characters" means "2 character points" | Treated as unresolved source wording; not silently corrected. | ChatGPT 5.5-high, Claude 5 Sonnet. | High |

## Section 7 — Governance and Authority Boundary

This report does **not**:

- Promote, demote, supersede, lock, unlock, close, reopen, or otherwise alter the status of any Tiwas material.
- Create a designer ruling.
- Close an open decision.
- Reopen a closed decision.
- Alter canonical status.
- Convert LLM agreement into authority.
- Treat the adventure as authority over Tiwas mechanics.
- Infer authority from chronology, majority, repetition, ordering, or apparent quality.
- Invent missing mechanics.
- Fabricate provenance.
- Silently reconcile conflicting evidence.

The report is an **advisory compilation only**. Any design decision arising from it remains subject to Tiwas governance and human designer authority.
